As his knowledge of the plant kingdom surpassed the limits of the knowledge of all his contemporaries, so his description of the beasts, birds, reptiles, and fishes was complete and exact.
When Solomon's surpassing knowledge appeared and news of it spread among the kingdoms of the world, kings and leaders of the world came to meet him and to enjoy hearing and seeing his wisdom.

Seize every opportunity to learn from the wisdom of others and to be a disciple at the hands of spiritual brothers, for because of your love of wisdom and your humility God pours out much upon you and you enjoy His work in you.
Preparation for building the Temple
Hiram: he is also called Huram in (2 Chr 2:3). Tyre: a great commercial city in Phoenicia, that is, Lebanon, lying on the coast of the Mediterranean Sea.

Hiram king of Tyre was a lover of David. So when he learned of his death, he sent senior men of state to console Solomon and congratulate him on assuming the throne in succession to his father, and to confirm the covenants of love and peace between the two of them and between their two peoples.
Put them under the soles of his feet: made them subject to him.

Solomon answered Hiram with a message in which he explained to him his father David's desire to build a house for the Lord, but his being occupied with many wars with the surrounding countries kept him from fulfilling his desire.

Here Solomon made the Gentiles, that is, Hiram, partners in the building of the house of God. He is a type of Christ, who made the Gentiles partners with the Jews in the temple of His body when He died for all, and gives all His true Body and Blood.
Solomon here is a type of Christ in the establishment of peace in his days, as Christ bound Satan after His victory over him by the Cross and gave peace to those who believe in Him.
Behold, I purpose to build an house: I have intended to build a house.

Solomon showed Hiram the stability and peace which his kingdom enjoyed, for there were no enemies or evildoers to harm the kingdom, which allowed him to decide to build a house for the Lord as God had charged David his father (2 Sam 7:12).
Cedar from Lebanon: huge, tall, evergreen trees that live long, and their wood is bitter, that is, not subject to decay, so they are suitable for building great buildings and can be painted.
The Sidonians: the inhabitants of Sidon, which lies north of Tyre and belongs to its king.

Solomon asked the king of Tyre to commission his men living in Sidon, which was under him, to cut cedar trees from Lebanon, and Solomon would send his men to work with the men of the king of Tyre, and he would pay the wages of the Sidonians as the king of Tyre determined, because the children of Israel were not skilled at cutting trees like the people of the city of Sidon. This shows Solomon's wisdom in making use of the talents of others in cooperating with him and his honesty in not exploiting them, but paying their wages as their king Hiram saw fit, that is, full wages. Solomon's importing of timber from Hiram and giving in return supplies such as wheat, barley, wine, and oil (2 Chr 2:10) was the economic exchange that resulted from the friendship between Tyre and the children of Israel and strengthened the bond between them.

How beautiful is cooperation! It lets you benefit from the experience of those around you and achieve greater success, but it needs humility, as Solomon, the owner of a great kingdom, humbled himself in his words to the king of Tyre. By humility you win those around you and achieve for yourself and for others what they desire.

Hiram welcomed taking part in the work with the son of his friend David, and saw that he was a good and wise son and a gift from God to the people of Israel. It was the custom of the pagans to believe that every country has its gods and that it is proper for each country to respect the god of the other, so he said "Blessed be the Lord," not because he believed in Him but out of mere respect.
Fir: a large tree found in Syria and Palestine, whose wood is used for building ships and building houses along with cedar wood.

Hiram responded to Solomon and agreed to supply him with all he wanted of cedar and fir timber. It is understood from this that Solomon asked for kinds of timber, not only cedar wood, but as the Book of Chronicles mentions, he asked for fir and algum wood (2 Chr 2:8).
Armathā: bundles.

Hiram added that he would order his men to cut the timber from the trees, gather it in bundles, throw them on the waters of the sea, and drive them floating on the surface of the waters, to deliver them to Solomon's men at the place Solomon would appoint, and from this place Solomon and his men could carry this timber overland to wherever he wanted. In return for the price of the timber Hiram sent him, Solomon sent Hiram the food supplies for his palace.
Measure (cor): a measure for liquids and grain whose volume is approximately 229 liters.
Wheat: grain.
Pure oil: it is the purest of oils because there are no impurities in it, since the oil is extracted by beating the fruit and not by pressing it.

Hiram carried out the agreement between him and Solomon, so Solomon obtained all his needs of cedar and fir timber from the king of Tyre, and in return supplied him with the food supplies he asked for, giving him each year, throughout the period of preparing the timber, twenty thousand measures of wheat and twenty measures of oil. This, of course, is apart from the wages of the workers belonging to Hiram, which are mentioned in (2 Chr 2:10), where we find a larger quantity of oil that Solomon provided.

We see by this that Solomon feeds his people the Jews working with him, and likewise the Gentiles belonging to the king of Tyre, with wheat, wine, and oil (2 Chr 2:10). In this he is a type of Christ, who feeds those who believe in Him, whether of Jewish or Gentile origin, with His Body and Blood taken from wheat and wine, and gives them His Holy Spirit, who is symbolized by the oil.

The Lord gave Solomon wisdom to maintain his friendship with Hiram, and both succeeded in keeping up relations of mutual affection, and they put that into a covenant that both of them made. The friendship between the two peoples continued until the reign of King Ahab, who married Jezebel the daughter of the king of Sidon (ch. 16:31). So we see that friendship with the surrounding peoples is beneficial, but care must be taken against an increase of closeness that leads the people of God to take on the customs of other peoples and worship their gods, as happened in the days of Ahab.

It is very useful to take care to make peace with those around you, for this lets you be occupied with your spiritual worship and your service, in addition to cooperating with them, so that love is established between you and them and you win everyone to God by your love and your working for their comfort.
The levy: the workers conscripted for work.

Adoniram: see the commentary on (ch. 4:6). Solomon put 30 thousand Israelites to work, sending them in rotation, 10 thousand at a time in a group that stayed to work for a month in Lebanon and returned, so that the men stayed in their houses with their families for two months until the time of the next turn came. This was Solomon's care not to burden the workers, and for the unity and well-being of the family, so that the worker's family would not feel deprived of him. He chose for the children of Israel the cutting of timber, while the non-Jews worked in cutting stones (v. 25); that is, he chose the easier work for his own people out of concern for them. Forced labor meant that a man worked in return for his food and necessary needs, and forced labor was known in great countries for the completion of huge projects, as in Egypt for the building of the pyramids. The treatment of those conscripted was good, especially of the children of Israel, for they were not considered slaves but as hired workers, and they gave a tax to the state for the completion of its great projects, which was part of their wages, because those who conscripted them were the men of war, the princes, and Solomon's assistants, as will come in (ch. 9:22). As for the other group that was conscripted, other than the children of Israel, they were the surrounding peoples subject to Solomon, and their forced labor was considered as tribute that they paid to the Jewish kingdom.

The number of workers was thirty thousand out of the total men of the children of Israel, whose number exceeded one million four hundred thousand, that is, a proportion of about 1 to 50. Of the thirty thousand, each ten thousand worked for a month and rested two months in his house to do his own work, such as farming; then the second group went for a month, then the third, and after that the turn of work returned to the first group, which had rested two months. The conscription was limited to the Jews for work outside the Jewish kingdom, that is, with King Hiram, because they would certainly return to their families and lands, while the conscription of the Gentiles was inside the Jewish kingdom, so that they would not flee if he sent them outside the land of Judea to Hiram.

Solomon appointed Adoniram as the one responsible for supervising the employment of the labor force, as was also mentioned before in (ch. 4:6). He had also held this post in the days of David, and because of his competence he continued in his work in the days of Solomon, and after that in the days of his son Rehoboam. But because forced labor is an undesirable thing, when Rehoboam sent him to quell a rebellion, they killed him.

Solomon set the number of burden-bearers in the transport of stones at seventy thousand and of those hewing stones at eighty thousand, all of them prisoners of war from the other nations, as will come in (ch. 9:20), (2 Chr 8:7-9). These did not have a system of rotation for rest as the Israelite workers did, because they were slaves.

The numbers mentioned in the previous verse are the numbers of the workers who carried burdens and cut stones. But the work needed other labor to supervise the execution, organize the work, distribute the workers, monitor performance, and control the movements of the labor force, and the number of these was 3300 overseers.

King Solomon commanded that the workers select the stones of large size and high quality from the mountains near Jerusalem, such as Mount Moriah, and prepare them to be squared and smooth, so that they would be suitable for building the house of the Lord.
The Giblites: the inhabitants of the city of Gebal, which lies on the Mediterranean Sea about 32 km north of Beirut.

Solomon's builders hewed the stones in cooperation with the builders of King Hiram, and the inhabitants of the coastal city of Gebal also took part with them, who had experience in building work in general and in shipbuilding in particular, and the builders also prepared the timber needed for the building.

Solomon provided the best materials for building the Temple and the best specialized workers. May we, in our worship of God, offer our best times, and in our giving offer the best we have to God, who gives us all good things, as a simple expression of our love and thanks to Him.
The building of the Temple. Note: see the drawings and pictures at the end of the book.

Solomon built the house of the Lord and called it the Temple, and that was on Mount Moriah (2 Chr 3:1), which lies in the eastern part of the city of Jerusalem, and in the same place Abraham took Isaac to offer him as a sacrifice to God (Gen 22:2). On Mount Moriah also was the threshingfloor of Araunah the Jebusite, where the angel stood to stop the spread of the plague in the days of David (2 Sam 24:15, 16). Solomon's Temple was built around the year 1000 BC and lasted until the year 586 BC, when the Babylonians destroyed it, and it was rebuilt after the return from the captivity at the beginning of the reign of the kingdom of the Medes and Persians by Zerubbabel in the year 536 BC; then the Greeks destroyed it and the Maccabees renewed it in the year 167 BC; then it was renewed again by Herod the Great in the year 20 BC and lasted until the year 70 AD, when Titus the Roman commander destroyed it, and it was not built afterward and will not be built, as Christ foretold when He said, "Behold, your house is left unto you desolate" (Mt 23:38).

entries.section: (1) The dimensions of the Temple, its stories, and its chambers

paragraphs.text: The month Zif: after the captivity its name became the month "Iyyar," which corresponds to part of the month of April and another part of the month of May. It is the second month of the religious year of the Jews, that is, the eighth month of the civil year.

The house: that is, the whole house of the Lord, and sometimes what is meant by it is the Holy Place, that is, the place that only the priests enter, which is in front of the Holy of Holies, in which the ark of the covenant is.

The writer of the book teaches us that the four hundred and eightieth year after the departure of the children of Israel from Egypt in the days of Moses corresponds to the fourth year of Solomon's reign. Solomon spent three years completing the gathering of building materials for the Temple, in addition to what he received of materials his father David had prepared, and he also took care in these three years to gather the workers who would build the Temple and to organize them. The four hundred and eighty years include forty years in the wilderness of Sinai in the days of Moses, then the entry of the children of Israel into the land of Canaan and their possession of it in the days of Joshua, then the age of the judges, and after it the age of the kingdom, that is, the kingdom of Saul and then David. The fourth year of Solomon's reign corresponds to about the year 1011 BC.

The building of the house began in the second month of the religious year of the Jews, and it was called the house of the Lord because it was set apart for the worship of the Lord, and He is the One who chose it and set its design.

It is noticed that the tabernacle of meeting is a type of the body of Christ on earth, that is, His body that would be changed, while Solomon's Temple is a type of the luminous body of Christ that remains forever. The tabernacle of meeting is a type of the Church on earth, because its ground is earthen, while Solomon's Temple is a type of the Church in heaven, because its floor is covered with gold, which is a symbol of heavenly things.

entries.section: (1) The dimensions of the Temple, its stories, and its chambers

paragraphs.text: The cubit: a unit for measuring lengths, equal to about 50 cm.
The house: what is meant by it is the whole Temple, that is, the Holy Place and the Holy of Holies.
Its height: that is, its elevation.
The dimensions of the Temple were double the dimensions of the tabernacle of meeting, and they were as follows:

Length 60 cubits, that is, about 30 meters; width 20 cubits, that is, about 10 meters; height 30 cubits, that is, about 15 meters. It is noticed that these measurements are the clear interior ones, without counting the thickness of the walls. These measurements and the details of the building of the Temple were made known by God to David, who made them known to his son Solomon (1 Chr 28:12). Even so, the dimensions of the Temple are small, because those who enter it are only the priests and high priests, while the outer court is wide, since the people enter it. As for the great height of the Temple, it was the usual thing at that time, since some temples of idols rose higher than this, such as the temple of Artemis at Ephesus.

entries.section: (1) The dimensions of the Temple, its stories, and its chambers

paragraphs.text: The porch: an entrance, or a roofed hall whose roof rests on columns.

The temple of the house: what is meant by it here is the Holy Place, which the priests enter, but sometimes what is meant is the whole house of the Lord. The word "temple" (haykal) is a Sumerian word meaning the great house, and the Sumerians are the ancient inhabitants of the land between the two rivers, that is, present-day Iraq.

There was a roofed hall with columns in front of the Temple, ten meters long and five meters wide. The Second Book of Chronicles adds that its height reached sixty meters (2 Chr 3:4). Solomon took care to make this porch tower to a great height, so that the appearance of the house would be very grand among all the buildings. The pagan peoples took care to build lofty temples for their gods, such as the Egyptians in their building of the temple of Karnak.

It is noticed that the entrance of the Temple, like the entrance of the tabernacle of meeting, was from the east, while the Holy of Holies, where the ark of the covenant of God was, was in the west; God intended this so that they would not be like the sun-worshipers. In the New Testament, the sanctuary of the Church is in the east, for the following reasons:
1- Because Paradise was in the east.
2- The star appeared to the magi in the east.
3- Christ was born in the land of Judea, that is, in the east.
4- Christ is the Sun of Righteousness, that is, the One who comes from the east.
5- Christ will appear at His Second Coming from the east, as He says that the lightning comes out of the east and shines even unto the west, so shall also the coming of Christ be.
That is, what is meant in the Church is to look toward Christ, who appeared in the east and will come at His Second Coming from the east.

entries.section: (1) The dimensions of the Temple, its stories, and its chambers

paragraphs.text: Windows: openings high in the north and south walls near the roof.
Broad: its roof is the thickness of the walls.
Narrow lights: over the windows were crossed wooden bars or bars of bronze, or of any metal, to prevent birds from entering.

Solomon made small windows in the walls of the house, that is, the Holy Place, and covered them with wooden or metal lattices to let air in or smoke out and at the same time to keep birds from entering.

entries.section: (1) The dimensions of the Temple, its stories, and its chambers

paragraphs.text: Stories: floors.
The oracle: the Holy of Holies.
Round about: that is, on the north, west, and south sides.

He built along the sides of the walls of the Holy Place and the Holy of Holies chambers surrounding them, in three stories one above the other, and each story, that is, floor, contained several rooms. These rooms were on the sides of the Temple, that is, the Holy Place and the Holy of Holies, on the north and south sides and also behind the oracle; that is, the rooms were around the Temple on three sides, and the remaining east side was the door, on which there were of course no rooms. These rooms were used for the needs of the Temple, as vessels, offerings, incense, tithes, and heave offerings were put in them, and they were for the priests' lodging and their meetings with the Levites and the scribes (Jer 36:10, 20). It is noticed that no one lived in the tabernacle of meeting or beside it, so that God might show His greatness and awe, so that everyone feared Him and no one could easily approach Him. But in Solomon's Temple God permitted the priests to dwell in His house, as a preparation for the Church of the New Testament, in which all the people are permitted to enter to receive His Body and Blood and be united with Him.

entries.section: (1) The dimensions of the Temple, its stories, and its chambers

paragraphs.text: Narrowed rests: plural of a rest, which is an angle or projection in the outer wall of the rooms, since the wall decreases in thickness at the end of the story, leaving a space on which the ends of the timbers can be placed; that is, the wall is thick at the first story, decreases in thickness at the middle story, and again at the upper story.
Beams: wooden columns, that is, rafters, laid close together to form the ceiling of the room, or the floor of the room above it.

When the walls of the Temple were built, the wall was built thick at the bottom, and at a height of five cubits, that is, at the story following it, he made the thickness of the wall decrease by half a cubit, then after another five cubits of height he made the wall of the Temple decrease by half a cubit up to the roof of the Temple. The same measurements were followed exactly in the opposite wall, that is, the outer wall of the rooms.

When building the rooms, Solomon did not want to dig into the walls of the Temple to set the boards forming the roof of the rooms, or the floor of the rooms above them, so as not to weaken the walls of the Temple.

So he built the wall of the Temple, which is the inner wall of the rooms, and likewise the outer wall, thick at the bottom, and at a height of five cubits, that is, at the middle story, the thickness of each of the two walls decreases by half a cubit, and thus a space, that is, a projection, is formed in each of the two walls on which the wooden boards are placed, and this is repeated after another five cubits, that is, at the upper story.

By this the width of the lower rooms is five cubits, then in the middle story it increases to become six cubits, and in the upper it increases to become seven cubits. So the higher we go, the more the area of the room increases.

entries.section: (1) The dimensions of the Temple, its stories, and its chambers

paragraphs.text: Hammer: an iron tool for breaking and hewing stones (a pick). Axe: a hatchet.

The house was built with whole stones which the workers quarried and hewed in their quarries, that is, in the places from which they were cut, before being brought to the site of the Temple, so that no sound of any iron tool for hewing and dressing the stones was heard in the Temple while it was being built. This means that the work was done in the house of the Lord quietly. That was in fulfillment of God's commandment not to use iron tools in building His altar or His Temple, so that they would not resemble the temples of idols in which these tools are used to make statues (Ex 20:25). The stones are a type of the believers built up as living stones in the body of Christ, that is, the Church, and the hewing of the stones is a type of the sufferings that the believers endure on earth, while in the Temple, which is a type of heaven, there is no hewing in it, that is, no sufferings in it.

entries.section: (1) The dimensions of the Temple, its stories, and its chambers

paragraphs.text: Winding stairs: a spiral stair.

The means of going up to the middle story and then the upper was through an entrance in the middle room, that is, the one in the middle of the rooms on the right side of the house, the south side, so that the entrance is on your right if you are looking to the east. From this entrance we find a spiral stone stair going up to the middle story, and from it to the upper story.

entries.section: (1) The dimensions of the Temple, its stories, and its chambers

paragraphs.text: After Solomon finished building the house, he covered its roof with beams and boards of cedar wood.

entries.section: (1) The dimensions of the Temple, its stories, and its chambers

paragraphs.text: Their height: their elevation.
They rested: were fastened.
Solomon built the chambers with a height of five cubits, that is, 2.5 meters for each story, so that the height of the three stories is 15 cubits, apart from the thickness of the roofs and floors.

The fastening of the chambers to the house with cedar beams, as we explained in (v. 6), was by setting the beams on the rests, that is, the angles or projections formed as a result of the decrease in the thickness of the walls, so that they rested on them and were strong without the need for any digging in the wall of the house.

The firmness of the chambers and their attachment to the Temple is a type of the servants who are steadfast in the Church and help in gathering souls to cleave to God. So take care to be steadfast in the Church through the Holy Sacraments and the means of grace, so that you can help others to be bound to the Church and enjoy God's care.

entries.section: (2) The word of the Lord to Solomon at the time of building the Temple

paragraphs.text: During the building of the house, while Solomon was devoting all his energies and the energies of the kingdom to building the Temple of the Lord, the Lord spoke to him, either in a vision, or through Nathan the prophet, or one of the prophets, for the following reasons:
1- To encourage him, because the work was huge, so that he would feel that God was with him, helping him and completing everything for him, especially since Solomon was young.

2- To alert him that keeping the commandment is more important than building the house, so he and his people should hold fast to the commandments of God during the building of the house and afterward.

entries.section: (2) The word of the Lord to Solomon at the time of building the Temple

paragraphs.text: I will perform my word: I will carry out what I have pledged.

The Lord assured him that if he and the people remained faithful in their conduct, keeping the worship of God and His law, and observed all His commandments to do them, then on His part He would fulfill for them all that He had promised David his father, and would dwell among them and not forsake them.

God wants to dwell among us because He loves us and wants to satisfy us with His love and shepherd us. Do we make room for Him in our hearts and give up everything that keeps us from Him .. He wants us to be holy temples for Him in which prayers rise like the fragrance of incense, so that He blesses us with every spiritual blessing we need.

entries.section: (3) The Holy Place and the Holy of Holies

paragraphs.text: Thus Solomon built the Temple of the Lord and finished building it, that is, its outer walls and its roofs of stones and timber, and then it will mention after this the covering of the house on the inside with timber and gold and then adorning them.

entries.section: (3) The Holy Place and the Holy of Holies

paragraphs.text: Ribs: boards.

After the stone walls were built, Solomon wanted to cover them with timber on the inside, so he set up ribs, that is, wooden uprights from the floor to the roof, and then fastened wooden boards to these uprights, which covered the whole wall, and no one could see the stone inside the Temple any longer. The timber lining the walls was of precious cedar wood, which does not spoil or wear out easily, while the floor of the Temple he covered with boards of fir wood, which is also among the precious timbers.

entries.section: (3) The Holy Place and the Holy of Holies

paragraphs.text: The sides of the house: that is, the western part of the Temple, which is a cubic part whose length, width, and height are twenty cubits, that is, ten meters.

He even built it within for the oracle: he set apart this part, that is, the rear of the house, to be the place for the Holy of Holies, which he called the oracle, for the ark of the covenant to be put in it; the word "oracle" (mihrab) is applied to the inner chambers in temples, and it is a Greek word meaning the place that one is permitted to enter. Solomon set apart ten meters of the rear of the house for the Holy of Holies and covered its walls entirely from the floor to the roof with boards of cedar wood, and set up a wooden wall from the floor to the roof to separate the Holy Place from the Holy of Holies, and made a door in it, as appears from (v. 31).

entries.section: (3) The Holy Place and the Holy of Holies

paragraphs.text: The rest of the Temple extended in front of the Holy of Holies for a length of 20 meters, and it is the part called the Holy Place, in which are the lampstand, the altar of incense, and the table of the showbread, and only the priests enter it, and it lies on the eastern side of the Holy of Holies.

entries.section: (3) The Holy Place and the Holy of Holies

paragraphs.text: Carved: engraved by carving.

All the walls of the house on the inside were covered with timber, and on them were carved, for adornment, shapes of flowers and gourds, because God rejoices in the spiritual fruits of His children who worship Him, which are symbolized by the flowers and gourds.

entries.section: (3) The Holy Place and the Holy of Holies

paragraphs.text: Oracle: the Holy of Holies.

He prepared an oracle in the midst of the Temple within, in which to put the ark of the covenant of the Lord, since the entrance of the oracle was through the Holy Place, and the oracle was surrounded by the chambers on its three sides, north, west, and south, while the east side was the Holy Place. So the oracle is in the middle because it is surrounded by chambers on three sides, and the fourth side is the Holy Place.

The scholar Origen says: "The soul must have an altar in the midst of the heart on which we offer the sacrifices of prayer and the giving of mercy, and on which we slay every evil thought and kill all pride and anger." Let your heart be a sacrifice of the love of God, from which prayers and praises rise every day, and let it be moved with love and kindness toward everyone in need.

entries.section: (3) The Holy Place and the Holy of Holies

paragraphs.text: The length, width, and height of the oracle were ten meters. He covered it with plates of pure gold and beat the gold onto the carved, engraved wood, so that the whole wall appeared as gold engraved with the decorative shapes that were carved on the wood beneath it, and the gold plates were fastened to the wood with gold nails, and therefore nothing was seen inside the oracle but gold, to declare the greatness of the presence of God. Gold also symbolizes heavenly life, so it declares that God's dwelling is in heaven and that in His humility He dwelt among His people, to lift them up and raise them above all earthly desires.

The altar of incense, made of stone, which was in the Holy Place, Solomon overlaid with cedar wood and then overlaid the wood with gold. This is the golden altar, that is, the altar of incense on which incense is offered every day inside the Holy Place before the oracle, that is, the Holy of Holies. It is noticed that this altar in the tabernacle of meeting was made of acacia wood and overlaid with gold because it was carried with the equipment of the tabernacle, while here, for the permanence of the Temple, it was made of stone (Ex 30:1-8).

entries.section: (3) The Holy Place and the Holy of Holies

paragraphs.text: In this way Solomon covered the whole Temple on the inside with pure gold, that is, the stone walls covered with timber and likewise the wooden wall separating the Holy Place from the Holy of Holies, the wooden one made in it. So nothing was seen inside the Holy Place and the Holy of Holies but gold. He drew chains of gold before the door, which are lifted only once a year, so that the priests might enter through this main door on the great Day of Atonement (Lev 16). From the above appears the tight closing of the Holy of Holies to show the glory of God, which no one can behold. Only the high priest is permitted once a year, as a type of Christ our High Priest, who ascended into heaven once after His Resurrection to prepare a place for us and take us to Himself, which is the Kingdom of Heaven. The way into the holiest in the Old Testament was closed because of our sins, and Christ the Redeemer opened it in the New Testament to bring us with Him into heaven. It is noticed that the oracle, which is the Holy of Holies, has no windows, because it is a type of heaven, which has no need of the sun or the moon for their rays to enter through the windows, because Christ is the light of heaven. The only light in the Holy of Holies was a divine light called the light of the Shekinah, which the high priest sees between the two cherubim that are on the ark.

entries.section: (3) The Holy Place and the Holy of Holies

paragraphs.text: The altar that was by the oracle: the altar of incense, which is in the Holy Place, which is called the house and is in front of the Holy of Holies, which is called the oracle, and incense is raised upon it before the oracle; therefore it was called the altar of the oracle.

The whole Temple was overlaid on the inside with pure gold, including the altar of the oracle, and this required large quantities of gold. David had left Solomon a great amount of gold (1 Chr 22:14), in addition to Solomon's income of gold, which was 666 talents in one year (ch. 10:14). Gold was used only rarely for minting gold coins. So Solomon had large quantities of gold available to build the house of the Lord.
This shows the following:
1- Solomon's care that the Temple of God be furnished with the finest materials, which was gold, at that time, out of his feeling that it was the greatest place in the world.
2- To help the priests during their service to feel reverence before God and a sense of His presence.
3- Gold symbolizes heavenly life, so it gives the priests a sense of longing for heaven, where the throne of God is.

The overlaying of the Temple with gold shows the extent of Solomon's love and care for the house of the Lord, and it gladdens God's heart that you offer Him the dearest thing you have, and if you have only little, God rejoices in your gifts however small they are, like the gift of the widow with the two mites. What matters is that you show your love for God by giving as much as you can.

entries.section: (3) The Holy Place and the Holy of Holies

paragraphs.text: Two cherubim: the dual of cherub, an angel of the rank of the cherubim or sharubim who are full of eyes, and who represents divine justice.

Solomon made two cherubim, the height of each ten cubits, and their wings spread on their two sides, and from the tip of the wing of the cherub to the other tip ten cubits. He set up the two cherubim next to each other, so that the tip of the wing of one cherub touched the tip of the wing of the other cherub. The two cherubim stood on the floor of the Holy of Holies, and the tip of the wing of each cherub reached the wall, that is, the cherubim reach between the north and south walls and stand beside the ark and look toward the Holy Place, which is called the house; they represent divine justice. When the high priest sprinkles the blood on the ark on the great Day of Atonement every year, the two cherubim, that is, divine justice, see the blood and God pardons His people. The blood of animals, as we know, is a type of the blood of Christ the Savior, by which we obtain forgiveness.

The two cherubim were made of olive wood, which is among the finest timbers. From the olive comes the oil, which is a type of the Holy Spirit, and the olive leaf is a type of peace; that is, the two cherubim are a type of the Spirit of God, who by the blood of Christ is pleased with us and forgives our sins and gives us peace. And because the dimensions of the Holy of Holies, which is called the oracle, are twenty cubits in length and twenty cubits in width, the two cherubim fill the whole space from the north wall to the south, while the roof is twenty cubits high and the height of the cherub is ten cubits, so their height is half the height of the oracle.

Then he overlaid the two cherubim with gold, because they are angels who symbolize heavenly life, since, as we mentioned, gold symbolizes heaven, so they declare that the oracle is an image of heaven on earth.
These two cherubim are different from the two cherubim on the cover of the ark, and they differ from them in the following:
1- These two cherubim stand on the floor, while the other two are on the cover of the ark.

2- The face of these two cherubim is turned toward the Holy Place, while the other two look toward the cover of the ark, where the blood is sprinkled, and divine justice, which is represented by these two cherubim above the cover, is satisfied. But these two cherubim standing on the floor have their faces toward the Holy Place, to declare the justice of God and His awe before those standing in the Holy Place.
3- These two cherubim are made of wood and overlaid with gold, while the other two are made of gold and are one piece with the cover.

4- The wings of these two cherubim standing on the floor extend from wall to wall, and the wing of each touches the other, so they are the front that the high priest sees when he enters the Holy of Holies, while the two sculpted cherubim on the cover look down toward the cover and the tips of their wings touch, so their form is arched, while the two on the floor are flat in form.

The Church is the image of heaven on earth; in it we receive the Body and Blood of the Lord to be united with us, so that He lifts our eyes to heaven that we may live for God and not for the world. So enter the Church with submission, knowing that you stand before God, and bow down before His sanctuary and thank Him for His grace that He has brought you into His house.

entries.section: (4) The adornment of the Temple and the time of its building

paragraphs.text: The house: what is meant by it here is the Holy Place and the Holy of Holies.

On all the walls of the Temple he carved drawings of cherubim, palm trees, buds, and flowers, on the inside of the Temple, that is, in the house and the oracle, which are the Holy Place and the Holy of Holies, and also on the outside, that is, on the walls of the outer porch in front of the house (v. 3). The cherubim, as we mentioned, their presence symbolizes the angels and heavenly life within the house of the Lord. Palm trees in the wilderness protect dwellings and tents, so they symbolize protection, security, and peace.

The buds and flowers symbolize the spiritual fruits that the Holy Spirit gives to His children who worship Him. When the priests and the people see these drawings, they are encouraged in spiritual striving to adorn themselves with virtues.
The carving of the cherubim, palm trees, buds, and flowers was engraved in the wood and then covered with gold, so they became golden carvings that everyone who enters the Holy Place sees.

entries.section: (4) The adornment of the Temple and the time of its building

paragraphs.text: He overlaid the floor of the Temple, made of fir wood, with gold, both inside, that is, in the Holy of Holies, and outside, that is, in the Holy Place, to declare the heavenly glory of God, and everyone who enters the house of the Lord feels submission before Him and awe of Him.

entries.section: (4) The adornment of the Temple and the time of its building

paragraphs.text: Leaf: a door leaf.
Lintel: the upper post of the door.
The side posts: the two side posts in which the door is fixed.
A fifth part: equal to a fifth of the width of the wall.

There was a wooden wall separating the Holy Place from the Holy of Holies (v. 21), in which Solomon made a door of two leaves whose width was a fifth of the width of the wall, that is, its width was four cubits; that is, each leaf with its side post fastened to it was two cubits wide.

entries.section: (4) The adornment of the Temple and the time of its building

paragraphs.text: He made the two leaves of the door of olive wood and carved on them drawings of cherubim, palm trees, and buds of flowers, then covered the two leaves of the door with gold, so that the carved shapes in the door and the projecting parts appeared in it, and their form was very beautiful, that is, inlaid with gold.

entries.section: (4) The adornment of the Temple and the time of its building

paragraphs.text: The door of the temple: that is, the outer entrance of the Holy Place, which is on the east side.
Squared: that is, the width of the door was a quarter of the width of the wall; the wall was twenty cubits wide, so the width of the door with its posts was five cubits.
Two folding leaves: the door leaf consisted of two leaves joined by hinges, one folding upon the other.

The entrance of the Temple, that is, the house or the Holy Place, consisted of a wooden wall in which a door was made five cubits wide, and the door had two leaves, each leaf made up of two sections folding one upon the other, so that the door opened fully. The door of the Holy Place was wider than the door of the Holy of Holies, because the priests enter the Holy Place every day, so its width was five cubits, while the Holy of Holies was four cubits wide, since only the high priest enters it, once a year. It is noticed that all the timber of the door was of the precious kind, which is olive wood or fir.

entries.section: (4) The adornment of the Temple and the time of its building

paragraphs.text: Spread: beaten out.

He carved on the two leaves the carving of cherubim, palm trees, buds, and flowers and overlaid them with beaten gold, so the shapes of the cherubim and the rest of the carvings appeared as though sculpted and made of gold, and they were very beautiful. It is understood from this that the gold was thin sheets that could be beaten to take the shape of the carvings engraved in the wood, so the shapes appear as though made of gold.

entries.section: (4) The adornment of the Temple and the time of its building

paragraphs.text: In front of the Holy Place there was the inner court, also called the court of the priests, a courtyard in which were the bronze altar and the lavers, and it had two walls on its sides. Each wall was made of three rows of stones laid one above another with a row of cedar wood on top of them to fasten and adorn them. This court is distinct from another court after it called the court of the people, or the outer court, or the great court. And let us not forget that in the tabernacle of meeting there was only one outer courtyard in front of the Holy Place. The court of the priests is called the upper court (Jer 36:10), because it was on a higher level than the court of the people, so that the people could watch the priests as they performed the various rites of worship (2 Chr 4:9).

entries.section: (4) The adornment of the Temple and the time of its building

paragraphs.text: The month Zif: corresponds to the months of April and May, that is, it takes a part of both months.
The month Bul: corresponds to the months of October and November.

The building of the Temple began in the fourth year of Solomon's reign in the month of Zif and continued until the eleventh year of his reign in the month of Bul, that is, it took seven and a half years, because it began in the month of Zif, which is the second month of the fourth year, and continued to the month of Bul, which is the eighth month of the eleventh year, so the period is seven years and six months, apart from the period of preparing the timber and materials with which the house was built. We see that Solomon made everything inside the Holy Place, or outside it, new, with measurements different from those in the tabernacle of meeting, but the only thing he did not change from the tabernacle of meeting was the ark of the covenant of God, which he took as it was and placed in the oracle, which is the Holy of Holies, for it represents the presence of God, and with God there is no variableness, neither shadow of turning.
It is noticed that the work on the Temple had a spirit distinct from the other works, the most important points of which are:
1- Care and enthusiasm, for they worked energetically because it was the house of God, that is, more important than any other house in the world.
2- The work was done with precision according to the specifications God declared and not according to the ideas of men, however artistic they were.

3- Quietly, for the timber and stones were not cut at the building place and the sound of a chisel was not heard, so the work was done quietly, and this suits the works of God, since they must be far from noise.
4- The work was done with joy because it is a great blessing for everyone who works in the house of the Lord.

The tabernacle of meeting declares the presence of God among His people, and its extension is Solomon's Temple; it is a type of the Church in the New Testament, and all of it is a type of the heavenly Jerusalem, that is, the Kingdom of Heaven, for all of it declares the presence of God among His people. The difference between the Church and Solomon's Temple is that it was not permitted for anyone but the priests to enter the Holy Place, and as for the Holy of Holies, the high priest alone enters it once a year, while in the Church all the people enter it, and even partake of the Body and Blood of the Lord and are united with Him, and the Church receives all believers whether of Jewish or Gentile origin.

Solomon's Temple has hidden parts that no one sees but the high priest, namely the Holy of Holies or oracle, while in the Church of the New Testament everything is open to the believers on earth, and the only hidden part is the triumphant Church in heaven, and even this appears to some believers in the appearances of the saints. And as the shapes of the cherubim were drawn on the walls of the Temple and its doors, so the angels fill the Church and surround the believers.

God's love has made you a temple of the Holy Spirit, so that God may dwell in you always by His Holy Spirit and give you His Body and Blood to be united with Him. You are prepared for God's dwelling, and to dwell in heaven; so remember this always, so that you keep away from every sin and draw near to God and enjoy fellowship with Him.
Solomon builds his palace and prepares the components of the Temple. Note: see the drawings and pictures at the end of the book.

The building of the Temple of the Lord took seven years, while Solomon built his palace in 13 years. The number seven symbolizes perfection, for God rested on the seventh day of the creation of the world, and Solomon built the Temple with all perfection and precision. The speed of the building of the Temple compared with the time taken to build his palace is due to the fact that King David had prepared much for the building of the Temple, and also that the area of Solomon's own dwelling was larger than the area of the Temple, in addition to the fact that Solomon's concern was to build the house of God before his own house, so he mustered for it a huge number of workers who worked with energy and great joy for God. They were worn out in building the house of the Lord, so their number became smaller and their energy also less. For all this, the building of Solomon's palace, or his houses, took more time than the time of building the Temple.

What is meant by Solomon's house is a group of houses connected to one another for his dwelling and for administrative work and military preparations, in addition to a house for women, that is, the house of Pharaoh's daughter.

Solomon spent three years in preparing for the building of the Temple, then seven years in building it, and thirteen years in building his house on the hill called Zion, and after that he had only seventeen years left to manage his affairs in his palaces. After that he turned his attention to trade and to acquiring horses, chariots, and many marriages, and this was at the expense of his care for raising his many sons, and this appeared in his son Rehoboam, who was not wise, so that the kingdom was split at the beginning of his reign.
The forest of Lebanon: the forests of Lebanon.
Beams: cross-beams or wooden rafters.

Solomon built his houses south of the Temple on the same mountain on which the Temple was built, which is called Mount Zion, or Mount Moriah, or the city of David, and he describes in detail the first of these buildings, which is called the house of the forest of Lebanon. It is a building about 50 meters long, 25 meters wide, and fifteen meters high. It was called the forest of Lebanon because the timber used in its construction was cedar of Lebanon. Its roof was built of beams, that is, long timbers of cedar wood, and these beams, or cross-beams, rested on four rows of columns made of cedar wood, across the width of the building, which is twenty-five meters, and the rows extend the length of the building, which is fifty meters, with a large number of columns, the number of which is not mentioned.
Light: a small window.

The house of the forest of Lebanon contained 45 rooms divided among three stories, that is, each story contained fifteen rooms. The rooms of each story were divided as follows: six rooms along each side of the house lengthwise and three rooms across its width, and the roofs of all the rooms were of cedar wood. The rooms were distributed along three sides of the hall, and the fourth side is the entrance, that is, in the shape of the letter U, and all the rooms look out onto the hall.

In each room there was a window looking out on the outer courtyard, with another window in the same room opposite it looking out on the inner hall of the house, and the windows of the rooms on the right side of the house faced and were in line with the windows in the rooms on the left side of the house. The windows in the three stories were one above the other on a single line. All this gives good ventilation and lighting to the rooms and the inner hall. The house of the forest of Lebanon is the administrative building, through which Solomon managed the affairs of the kingdom using its many rooms, in addition to its being storehouses for weapons.
Square: that is, its upper surface straight and not round in the shape of an arch.
Covered: that is, the upper lintel, which is the upper frame of the door, whose width is the thickness of the wall, so that the thickness of the wall becomes a roof for the door.

He describes the doors of the house as square, with wooden posts on both sides of the door in which the leaves are fixed, and the width of the roof of the door was the thickness of the wall. He emphasizes here that the windows were one above the other in the three stories.
A porch of pillars: a hall that is the entrance of the building, roofed and resting on columns.

Thresholds: plural of threshold, which is the upper or lower lintel, and what is meant here is the lower lintel. There was a hall called the hall of pillars because of the many columns in it, about 25 meters long and about 15 meters wide, and in front of it was another hall, also with columns, and at the end of the second hall were several steps (a stair). The second hall was prepared here to be an entrance to the third porch, in which Solomon's throne was placed (v. 7). Neither the porch of pillars nor the other porch in front of it had walls, but columns bearing a roof, and all of it was made of cedar wood.

Solomon made a porch, that is, a hall with three walls and an entrance on the fourth side, and it was called the porch of the throne, that is, Solomon's throne, where he sat upon it to judge the various affairs of the kingdom. He covered the walls of the hall from the floor to the roof with cedar wood. He made this porch splendid, with walls covered with precious timber, to befit the king's council.

It is understood from the above that Solomon made a hall with columns, the porch of pillars, and this hall leads to another hall which also has columns, and at the end of this other hall there are several steps (a stair) leading to the porch of the throne or of judgment, where Solomon sits to judge.

Solomon built a house for his dwelling in front of the porch of judgment and connected to it, so there is no separation between the porch of judgment and the king's palace. He also built a house next to it for the residence of Pharaoh's daughter, which is the house of the women. The Temple was to the north of these houses. The building of Solomon's house and the house of Pharaoh's daughter was like the building of the house of the forest of Lebanon and the porch of judgment, that is, with the same kind of stones and timber.

Solomon's care in building a house for the women or for Pharaoh's daughter is a type of Christ, who took care to build a house for His bride, that is, the Church, and also of His receiving the Gentiles with the Jews.

There was the great court (v. 9), which surrounds all these buildings, that is, the house of the forest of Lebanon and the three porches, that is, the porch of pillars, the other porch, and the porch of the throne, then Solomon's house, the house of the women, and the Temple. It is also called the outer court, or the great court; that is, it is a large courtyard surrounded by a wall, and inside it all the preceding buildings.

Within the great court there is another court, which is the middle court, and it surrounds Solomon's house and the house of Pharaoh's daughter (the house of the women). After the middle court is the inner court, which surrounds the Temple, the court of the priests, and the court of the people (see the drawing of Solomon's buildings at the end of the book).
The cornice: the top of the wall next to the roof.

Solomon took care to build all these preceding buildings of large stones, not cut with axes but with special saws so that they were even on all sides, and he covered them with cedar wood, with complete precision.

Solomon also took care in building the foundations of these buildings, which were huge stones four or five meters long, and they were good, the same stones that were used in the rest of the building, and so the buildings were founded in a good manner to rise to enormous heights with the utmost safety.

This shows Solomon as a type of Christ, who builds His house, that is, the Church, which is also His body, with all precision by the work of His Holy Spirit and founded on His precious blood shed on the wood of the Cross.

Take care of the foundation of your life, that is, your faith in God and your holding fast to the Church and its sacraments, so that you have a strong spiritual building, virtues, and good relationships, and are successful with people as long as you are strong in your relationship with God.
The huge stones used in the walls were also hewn according to specified measurements and were covered with boards of cedar wood.
The porch of the house: that is, the porch of the house of the Lord.

The great court that surrounds all these buildings had its walls formed of three rows of hewn stones covered with boards of cedar wood in a manner similar to the inner court that surrounds the Temple, and likewise the middle court that surrounds Solomon's house and the house of Pharaoh's daughter (the house of the women); that is, the stones are laid one above another in the building of the wall and covered on top with blocks of cedar wood to protect them, bind them, and fasten them.

entries.section: (2) Hiram makes the bronze components of the Temple

paragraphs.text: Solomon summoned from Tyre one of the most skilled workers in bronze, Hiram, the son of a widow of the tribe of Naphtali, whose father was a Gentile. He had wide experience and complete understanding of the manufacture of bronze things, so he came to Solomon and did all the work that Solomon assigned to him. Perhaps, because his mother was a Jewess, Hiram took care to complete the works assigned to him with precision. This Hiram is different from Hiram king of Tyre.

God allowed this man of Gentile origin to work in His house, and this signifies that Christ is coming to save the Jews and the Gentiles. So know that God seeks the salvation of all, and do not despise anyone, however far away he is or however many his sins, for Christ seeks the salvation of the whole world.

entries.section: (3) The two pillars Jachin and Boaz

paragraphs.text: A line: a circumference.
The other: that is, the one pillar.

Solomon made two pillars and set them up before the Holy Place in the porch of the Temple (v. 21); the two pillars do not bear a roof but were made to adorn the Temple. He made them of bronze, and the length of each was nine meters and its circumference six meters. The pillar was hollow, and the thickness of its wall, that is, the thickness of the bronze it was made of, was four fingers (Jer 52:21), and the Book of Chronicles tells us that each pillar had a base four meters high (2 Chr 3:15).

entries.section: (3) The two pillars Jachin and Boaz

paragraphs.text: To show the greatness of the pillar and the greatness of the Temple in which it stood, he made for each pillar a capital of spherical shape. The height of the capital was two and a half meters, and this capital was also made of bronze.

entries.section: (3) The two pillars Jachin and Boaz

paragraphs.text: A network of bronze was made, and on it seven wreaths, also of bronze, to adorn the capital.

entries.section: (3) The two pillars Jachin and Boaz

paragraphs.text: He made for the capital two rows of bronze globes in the form of pomegranates, and the number of these pomegranates was a hundred in each row. Each pillar had two rows of pomegranates on the edges of the upper and lower networks, as also appears from (v. 42). That is, the base of the pillar bears a cylinder, and above the cylinder is a round row of pomegranates, and above it the ball of the capital, and on it the network on which are the wreaths, and above the capital a second round row of pomegranates, then the lily flower at the top of the pillar. So the base has the pillar above it, then the capital, then the lily flower.

entries.section: (3) The two pillars Jachin and Boaz

paragraphs.text: Of molten brass: the shape of the lily cast and formed of bronze.

He made above the capital the shape of a lily flower, which resembles the lotus flower. When it says in this verse "as in the porch," it means that the flowers carved on the door of the Holy Place, which are seen in the porch, were some of them in the shape of the lily flower (ch. 6:18). The height of the lily flower above the capital was two meters. The lily shape symbolizes purity and holiness, since Christ is likened in the Song of Songs to this flower (Song 2:1).

entries.section: (3) The two pillars Jachin and Boaz

paragraphs.text: It confirms here that the shape of the two capitals on the two pillars was the same.

entries.section: (3) The two pillars Jachin and Boaz

paragraphs.text: After he finished the two pillars, he set them up in the porch of the Temple and called one of them "Jachin," that is, Jehovah establishes or makes firm, and called the other pillar "Boaz," that is, Jehovah is mighty. It is clear from the height of the two pillars that they did not bear the roof of the house but were placed before the house for adornment and for spiritual meanings, which are:
1- The believer ought to be firm in the Church like the pillar, never moving, because salvation is within the Church and steadfastness is necessary for salvation.
2- By the believer's steadfastness within the house of God, he receives glory and might before God on earth and in heaven, as the two pillars were named Jachin and Boaz.
3- God rejoices in His children in His Church, for they adorn it with their prayers, like these two pillars adorned with the two capitals and the two flowers.
4- The believer ought to be adorned with virtues, which are symbolized by the pomegranates that cover the pillar and rise above it.

5- These two pillars were made of bronze, which is a symbol of spiritual striving on earth, and therefore the two pillars were placed in the porch, and when a person completes his striving he reaches the Kingdom of Heaven, where there are gold and the angels, that is, the cherubim, and this is what the Holy Place and the Holy of Holies symbolize.
6- God commanded the setting up of the pillars before the Holy Place because God is the One who sets up and establishes the believer by His grace in the house of the Lord.
7- The two pillars are a type of God's leading of His people, as He used to lead them in the wilderness by the pillar of cloud by day and the pillar of fire by night.
8- The capital in the form of a network symbolizes the believers' concern for catching souls and drawing them to the Church.

9- The pomegranate, whose taste is sharp, symbolizes spiritual striving, and its red color on the inside symbolizes the blood of Christ the Redeemer; that is, the pomegranate symbolizes the grace of Christ the Savior, who supports His striving children.
10- The two pillars are tall, so they symbolize the believer, who is a light to the world and shines like bronze, giving light to others and drawing others to God.

I wish that you would be steadfast in the sacraments of the Church and all its spiritual practices, so that you are adorned with many virtues and so do your work without knowing it, influencing those around you as they see Christ in you and love Him because of your spiritual conduct among them.
A line of thirty cubits did compass it round about: the circumference of the sea was 30 cubits, that is, about 15 meters.

He made a large basin of bronze for the priests to wash in, and called it the sea because of its large size compared with the laver that was in the tabernacle of meeting. This sea was round in shape, its upper mouth wider than its base, and its mouth in the form of a circle whose diameter was ten cubits, that is, five meters, and whose circumference was thirty cubits, that is, fifteen meters, and the height of the brim of this basin from the ground was five cubits, that is, two and a half meters.

He adorned the sea with two rows of gourd shapes, ten gourds to a cubit, and these two rows were under the brim of the sea, all made of bronze and cast of it. They symbolize the spiritual fruits with which the priest ought to be adorned, who washes in the water of the sea, as a sign of the purity with which he is clothed, in order to be able to carry out his service inside the house of the Lord, that is, the Holy Place.
Their hinder parts: the rear of their bodies.

He made the sea rest on 12 oxen made and cast of bronze, three oxen on each of the four sides, with their faces outward and their hinder parts inward, so the observer sees the faces of the oxen. The twelve oxen are a type of the twelve tribes of the children of Israel, for the priest enters the Holy Place after he is purified in the sea, to be a representative of all the believers in the service of God, that is, a representative of the twelve tribes. The twelve oxen are also a type of the twelve Apostles, by whom the world was preached to concerning the salvation of Christ, repentance, and Baptism. The faces of the oxen are outward so that the oxen, distinguished by strength, appear as a proclamation of the power of the priesthood.

Because the priests wash in the sea, it is a type of Baptism and repentance, by which we are able to stand before God; the ox is also a type of the sacrifice of Christ, and the blood of Christ is the foundation of salvation and the sacraments. The faces of the oxen are turned toward the four directions, three on each side, and the number three symbolizes the Holy Trinity, whom the Apostles preached in the four quarters of the world.
Bath: a measure for liquids equal to approximately 23 liters.
Thickness: its thickness.

The sea, which was in the shape of a basin, had a brim like the brim of the cup from which a person drinks, and the thickness of the wall of the sea was a handbreadth, that is, about 20 cm. Perhaps this brim was suitable for the priest to sit on when he goes up to the sea and goes down into it, and perhaps Solomon made a set of ladders or steps by which the priests went up or down inside the sea to wash, and the capacity of the basin was two thousand baths.

God in His love welcomes you greatly in His Church, but at the same time He is a great and awesome God. So you ought to be purified by repentance and confession, in order to be able to stand before Him and partake of His mysteries and enjoy fellowship with Him and His tenderness.

After that he made ten movable lavers (v. 38) on ten square bases, their length equal to their width, each of them two meters, and their height a meter and a half. These lavers were used to wash the flesh of the sacrifices (2 Chr 4:6).
Panels: square boards.
Ledges: plural of ledge, which is the frame or border in which the panel is set.

The base was a square bronze board with a frame surrounding it, cast with it as one piece, and on this board and its frame were shapes of lions, oxen, and cherubim. From the four sides of the frame hung bronze wreaths of flowers, made with precision.
The base was not only a flat board (v. 35) but in the form of a cart with four sides (like a handcart). The four side boards were adorned with the same drawings and wreaths.

These bases were made so that the lavers would rest upon them, and they were adorned with these shapes to declare God's authority over creation, such as the wild beasts, represented by the lions, the cattle, represented by the oxen, and the plants, represented by the flowers, and also over the heavenly beings, represented by the cherubim. They also declare that these sacrifices, which would be washed in these lavers, are offered for the purification of man and of all creation, so that everything may be clean and man's eyes may be lifted to heaven where the cherubim are. And also by these bloods we satisfy the justice of God, which the cherubim represent. The blood of animals is a type of the blood of Christ the Savior.
Wheels: the wheel.
Axletrees: a bronze rod that is the axis joining the two wheels, around which they turn.
Their feet: legs that come down from the four corners of the board of the base.
Undersetters: plural of shoulder, a reinforcement of the four corners of the board, rising upward to support the laver from its four sides and coming downward to form four legs of the base.

The four shoulders at the corners of the board of the base rose upward so that the laver would rest on them, and the extension of the shoulders downward formed four legs connected to the four wheels, and every two wheels turn around an axle to move the base with the laver when needed.
Beside the shoulders hung wreaths of flowers. And the base with everything in it was cast of bronze as one piece, to be solid.
Its mouth: a round opening in the center of the panel, a cubit in diameter.
The crown: a projection surrounding the opening, whose thickness was four cubits.

The board of the base was square, each side four cubits long (two meters), and in its center an opening was made, a cubit in diameter, surrounded by a frame, raised around the opening, and its thickness was a quarter of a cubit, so that the diameter of the opening and its frame was a cubit and a half. And because the board of the base was domed, as will come in (v. 35), it is mentioned here that the opening and its frame were raised.
On the crown surrounding its mouth were carvings like the carvings found in (v. 29).
Hooks: plural of hook, a curved piece of bronze.
The four legs of the base were joined to four hooks to connect to the four wheels. The diameter of the wheel was a cubit and a half (75 cm).
Their felloes: the outer rim of the wheel.

Their spokes: the wires or rods that connect the outer rim to the center of the wheel. Their naves: the circle in the center of the wheel, joined to the outer rim by the wires, through which passes the axle, or rod, that connects it to the opposite wheel.
The wheels were cast with all their parts, the rims, hooks, spokes, and naves, of bronze.
The four corners of the base had shoulders cast with the base and not attached to it, for increased strength (as came before in v. 30).
Domed: in the shape of a dome.

The upper board of the base was not flat but domed, and the height of the highest point of the dome was half a cubit, that is, 25 cm, and the base had hands for pulling it, cast of bronze with the base on its four sides as one part.
He carved cherubim, lions, palm trees, and wreaths of flowers on the handles and on the boards of the base, as far as there was room.
The ten bases were all of the same measurements and exactly identical, because they were all cast in succession in one mold.

If God cared for all this exactness in the making of the lavers in which the sacrifices of the Old Testament were washed, how much more ought you to be exact in preparing to partake of the Holy Mysteries, that is, of the sacrifice of Christ which gives you salvation, by repentance and confession and attending the Liturgy from its beginning and taking part in it with all your heart.

After that he made ten bronze lavers and set them above the ten bases, each laver on a base, and the capacity of each laver was 40 baths of water, and the diameter of the laver was two meters; this diameter was at the top, while at the bottom it was less than this so as to enter the opening in the base and remain in the base. There is another opinion, that the four cubits is the height of the laver and not its diameter (see the picture of the laver and the base at the end of the book).
Five bases were placed on the right side of the house, that is, toward the south, and five bases on the left side, that is, in the north, and the bronze sea was placed on the southeast of the house.
The shovels: plural of shovel, which is the scoop.

The basons: a bason is a hollow vessel used for sprinkling water or blood during the rites. Hiram and the team of skilled workers with him made the lavers, the shovels, and the instruments for sprinkling water, and he also completed all the requirements of the Temple as King Solomon decided for the house of the Lord.
The pots: vessels for cooking meat.
Bright: shining.
In these five verses is a list of the things Hiram made, and they are:
The two pillars
The two bowls of the capitals that were on the top of both pillars
The network covering the capital on both pillars
The four hundred pomegranates for the two networks, two rows of pomegranates for each network
The ten lavers and their movable bases.
The sea and the twelve oxen under it
The pots, the shovels, and the basons.
All of the above was made of bright bronze.

Solomon took care to do all the bronze works for the Temple of God with exactness. And God took care in the creation of your body with all precision, because it is a temple for His Holy Spirit, so whenever you move or breathe, thank God and keep your body pure and all your senses, so that the temple of God - which is your body - is fit for His dwelling.
The plain: a plain, or valley, that is, a low place.
Succoth: it lies east of the Jordan River at a distance of three miles.
Zarthan: it lies west of the Jordan River.

All the works of casting the preceding equipment and furnishings were done in the plain of the Jordan, in the area lying between Succoth, which lies east of the Jordan River, and Zarthan, which lies west of it, and which was called the land of clay because it is rich in the sand used in making the molds for casting the bronze equipment. Solomon intended that the casting of the bronze be done away from the area of the building of the Temple, so that it would be done with a precision suited to metalwork, and so that there would be no noise at the place of the Temple.

If the Temple is a type of the Kingdom, then the foundries are a type of the trials we meet on earth, because metals are cast by fire, and after the vessels are prepared with precision and are beautiful, they enter the Temple; so we, after being tested by trials, enter the Kingdom of Heaven.
Because of the multitude of the bronze works and the quantities of bronze used in them, Solomon could not count them exactly, and this shows:
1- That David had prepared large quantities of bronze.
2- Solomon supplemented these quantities generously, out of honor and care for the house of the Lord.
The flowers: shapes of flowers of gold on the head of the seven branches of each of the ten golden lampstands inside the house.
The lamps: a small vessel that is part of the lampstand, in which the oil and the wick are put to give light.
The tongs: plural of tongs, used to lift the used wicks and to put new wicks in the lampstands. The bowls: plural of bowl, that is, basin, used as a vessel for oil.
The snuffers: a tool like scissors for cutting off the burnt part of the wick.
The spoons: small dishes in which incense is put or in which fire is carried to the lampstands. The censers: plural of censer, that is, the shurriya.
The hinges: the hinges in the doors.
Solomon also took care of the golden vessels inside the house, that is, the Holy Place, and they are:
1- The altar of incense or the golden altar, which he made of stone and covered with cedar wood and then covered the wood with gold (ch. 6:20-22).
2- The table of the showbread.

3- Ten golden lampstands, five placed on the right of the house and five on its left before the Holy of Holies, that is, the oracle; and he made the flowers and the lamps that were on the lampstands all of gold.
4- The utensils used in the Holy Place such as the tongs, the bowls, the snuffers, the basons, the spoons, and the censers.
5- The hinges in the doors of the house and the oracle, that is, the Holy Place and the Holy of Holies.

It is noticed here that there were ten lampstands in the house, while in the tabernacle of meeting there was one lampstand (Ex 25:31). We also see that the altar of incense was made in the house of stone and covered with wood and gold, while in the tabernacle of meeting it was of wood covered with gold to make it easy to carry. And Solomon made the golden vessels of the house of the Lord by others than Hiram, who was a specialist in bronze work.
The vessels: the golden vessels that David won in his victories over the surrounding peoples.

All the requirements of the Temple and its building were supplied through King Solomon, who took all the gold and silver his father had prepared, which exceeded the need of the work of building the Temple, and put it in the treasuries of the house of the Lord and did not use it in his palace. David had taken care to collect the silver and gold which he took as spoils in his military victories over the countries surrounding him and had set it all apart for the building of the house of the Lord (2 Sam 8:9-11).

Solomon's care in building the Temple of the Lord urges us each to seek how to build within himself a dwelling for God, so that our bodies may be temples of God in which the Holy Spirit dwells, as St. Paul the Apostle called us to do (1 Cor 3:16). The dedication of the Temple (1) The transfer of the ark to the Temple (vv. 1-11:)

1- Then Solomon assembled the elders of Israel, and all the heads of the tribes, the chief of the fathers of the children of Israel, unto king Solomon in Jerusalem, that they might bring up the ark of the covenant of the LORD out of the city of David, which is Zion. 2- And all the men of Israel assembled themselves unto king Solomon at the feast in the month Ethanim, which is the seventh month. 3- And all the elders of Israel came, and the priests took up the ark. 4- And they brought up the ark of the LORD, and the tabernacle of the congregation, and all the holy vessels that were in the tabernacle, even those did the priests and the Levites bring up. 5- And king Solomon, and all the congregation of Israel, that were assembled unto him, were with him before the ark, sacrificing sheep and oxen, that could not be told nor numbered for multitude.
6- And the priests brought in the ark of the covenant of the LORD unto his place, into the oracle of the house, to the most holy place, even under the wings of the cherubims.
7- For the cherubims spread forth their two wings over the place of the ark, and the cherubims covered the ark and the staves thereof above.

8- And they drew out the staves, that the ends of the staves were seen out in the holy place before the oracle, and they were not seen without: and there they are unto this day. 9- There was nothing in the ark save the two tables of stone, which Moses put there at Horeb, when the LORD made a covenant with the children of Israel, when they came out of the land of Egypt. 10- And it came to pass, when the priests were come out of the holy place, that the cloud filled the house of the LORD, 11- So that the priests could not stand to minister because of the cloud: for the glory of the LORD had filled the house of the LORD.
The elders of Israel: they are the king's counselors, who help him in ruling in the cases of the people.
The heads of the tribes, the chief of the fathers: their number is 12, one for each tribe.

The city of David, Zion: it was first a fortress of the Jebusites, and afterward David took it and built in it a palace and a new city called by his name (1 Chr 11:4-8). The word Zion means "fortress," and it is one of the hills on which Jerusalem stands. David had brought the ark to it, and then Solomon moved the ark to the Temple that he built on Mount Moriah; that is, Zion is not Mount Moriah. Later the word Zion came to include the Temple as well, and the name Zion is often applied to the whole of Jerusalem.

The last place to which the ark had come was Zion, in a special tent that David pitched for it, which was different from the original tabernacle that Moses had made, which was set up at Gibeon and contained all the furnishings of the tabernacle. Since Solomon's Temple was built on Mount Moriah, it was natural that the ark be moved from Zion to the Temple to be placed in the Holy of Holies. It was fitting that the move take place in a festive manner, in a procession in which the elders of Israel and the heads of the tribes walked, whom King Solomon had invited to take part, for it was a celebration proclaiming God's dwelling in the midst of all the people and the dedication of the Temple. The word "bring up" does not mean moving the ark from a low place to a high place, but to the house of God, the greatest place in the world.

The month Ethanim: it is the seventh month in the Hebrew calendar of the religious year and the first month of the civil year, and it corresponds to September and October; the feasts of Atonement, Trumpets and Tabernacles fell in this month.

All the men of Israel answered the king's call, and all the religious and civil leaders and the representatives of the people took part in the celebration for moving the ark, which the king himself presided over, and this took place in the month of Ethanim.

The Temple had been completed in the month of Bul, that is, the eighth month, and Solomon waited eleven months, in which he finished the furnishings and the vessels inside the Temple and arranged everything connected with the celebration of the dedication of the Temple. He chose the seventh month of the following year because it is full of feasts, as we have mentioned, and the people gather in it from all the land as the Law prescribes. Thus, after about 480 years in which worship continued in the tabernacle of meeting, it now moved to a built and permanent Temple, Solomon's Temple.
The tabernacle: what is meant is the tabernacle that Moses made.

The priests carried the ark on their shoulders, as the Law prescribes. Carrying the ark was the work of the Levites, but because of the greatness of this celebration the priests themselves carried the ark. The tabernacle of meeting was at that time in another place outside Jerusalem, namely "Gibeon" (1 Chr 16:39), so all the furnishings and vessels that were in the tabernacle, and the tabernacle as well, were moved and kept in the chambers attached to the house of the Lord, because they had been sanctified by God's presence in them during the prayers, so they were a blessing that had to be preserved. Thus we understand that the ark was in one place, Jerusalem, while the tabernacle and its vessels were in Gibeon in the days of David, and all this was moved to the Temple.
