The tabernacle of meeting signifies the body of Christ in which He lived on earth, and the entry of the tabernacle into the house of God that Solomon built signifies the entry of Christ with His luminous body into heaven after His ascension.

In their procession before the ark, the king and the people offered sacrifices in numbers too many to be counted or numbered, to express their joy and their thanks to the Lord for His work with them and for His allowing a permanent Temple to be built in which He would dwell in their midst.
The priests brought the ark into the Holy of Holies and placed it in the place appointed for it under the wings of the cherubim made of olive wood overlaid with gold (ch. 6:27).
The wings of the cherubim overshadowed the ark, and the staves appointed for carrying the ark were in their places in the rings on the sides of the ark, until the ark was brought into its place.

After the priests brought in the ark with the two staves by which they carried it, they placed it under the wings of the cherubim standing in the Holy of Holies. Then they drew the two staves outward toward the door of the Holy of Holies, but did not remove them from the rings. They would shine when the high priest entered the Holy of Holies, in the divine light (the Shekinah) that shone at his entering; and so the shining of the ends of the staves could be seen, so that he would not come near the ark.

When the two staves were drawn out, the priests who were standing in the Holy Place at that time saw the ends of the two staves, and then they closed the door of the Holy of Holies, so that no one saw them any longer except the high priest when he entered once every year. The two staves were no longer used to carry the ark, because it had come to rest in the Holy of Holies and there was no need to move it, as used to happen in the past in the tabernacle of meeting. The tabernacle signifies the Church sojourning in the wilderness of the world, while the Temple signifies the heavenly Jerusalem, where the Church rests with Christ forever.

The presence of the two staves in their rings on the ark, although it had come to rest in the Holy of Holies, reminds us believers of the necessity of constant vigilance in our spiritual striving, which will not end until we enjoy entering eternal life. We must also always realize that we are strangers on this earth until we return to our heavenly home.

There was nothing inside the ark except the two tablets of the Law; as for the pot of manna and Aaron's rod, which the Apostle Paul mentioned in (Heb 9:4), they were placed in a special chest beside the ark in the sanctuary. The pot of manna and Aaron's rod used to be set in the tabernacle of meeting before the ark of the covenant (Num 17:10), and then placed in it when they set out on a journey; but in the Temple, after they had settled, they were placed before the ark in a special chest.

When the priests came out of the Holy Place after placing the ark in its place, a thick cloud appeared and filled the Temple, as a sign of God's satisfaction with what King Solomon and his people had done. The density of the cloud was extremely noticeable, so that the priests were not able to begin the service. This is the same thing that happened at the dedication of the tabernacle of meeting, when Moses was not able to enter (Ex 40:34-35). God did not appear in His glory until after the priests had gone out, because they could not bear to see the glory of God.

Note: the priests placed the ark of the covenant in the Holy of Holies and then went out before the beginning of the service, and after that no one was permitted to enter the Holy of Holies except the high priest, and only once a year. The glory of God appeared in the form of a cloud for the following reasons:
1- The cloud is high in the sky, and God is exalted above our thoughts and our works.
2- The cloud is pure water that evaporated and rose to the sky, and God is pure, indeed perfectly pure.
3- The cloud is white in color, and God is all radiance and majesty.
4- The cloud hides what is behind it, and God, no one knows the depths of His essence, because He is unlimited, and it is not possible to know all His thoughts and plans.

The cloud proclaims the presence of God in many places, as in the Transfiguration of Christ on the mountain. But the mystery of the appearing of the cloud proclaims the glory of God and His esteem for this Temple, and His appreciation of the labor of Solomon and all his people in building it with such magnificence; and the true mystery of greatness is the indwelling of God, not the splendor of the building.

The glory of the Lord, when it filled the house, signifies the body of Christ in the fullness of time, and also the dwelling of His Holy Spirit in the heart of every believer in the New Testament, in addition to His dwelling in His Church and His Holy Sacraments. (2) The fulfillment of God's promise (vv. 12-21)

12- Then spake Solomon, The LORD said that he would dwell in the thick darkness. 13- I have surely built thee an house to dwell in, a settled place for thee to abide in for ever. 14- And the king turned his face about, and blessed all the congregation of Israel: (and all the congregation of Israel stood;) 15- And he said, Blessed be the LORD God of Israel, which spake with his mouth unto David my father, and hath with his hand fulfilled it, saying, 16- Since the day that I brought forth my people Israel out of Egypt, I chose no city out of all the tribes of Israel to build an house, that my name might be therein; but I chose David to be over my people Israel. 17- And it was in the heart of David my father to build an house for the name of the LORD God of Israel. 18- And the LORD said unto David my father, Whereas it was in thine heart to build an house unto my name, thou didst well that it was in thine heart. 19- Nevertheless thou shalt not build the house; but thy son that shall come forth out of thy loins, he shall build the house unto my name. 20- And the LORD hath performed his word that he spake, and I am risen up in the room of David my father, and sit on the throne of Israel, as the LORD promised, and have built an house for the name of the LORD God of Israel.
21- And I have set there a place for the ark, wherein is the covenant of the LORD, which he made with our fathers, when he brought them out of the land of Egypt.

Solomon stood to encourage the people, since their hearts were filled with awe when the glory of the Lord filled the house with the cloud, and he made his people understand that the cloud is a proclamation of God's presence in the midst of His people and His dwelling in His house. God had appeared in the cloud before that, in the days of Moses the prophet, and it seems that this expression, that is, God's dwelling in the cloud, was known among the Jews, since they used to see it settle upon the tabernacle of meeting; but Solomon confirms it here, when he saw the cloud covering the house of the Lord at its dedication.

Solomon began a sermon that is in essence a hymn of thanksgiving to God for what He permitted by fulfilling the desire of David his father, enabling his son Solomon to build a house in which the Lord would dwell forever.

Solomon's face had been toward the Holy of Holies when the ark was brought into it, so he turned around to face his people standing before him and to bless them with the blessing with which the high priest blesses the people, as Moses the prophet blessed them (Ex 39:43) and as David did when he brought up the ark of the Lord to the city of David (2 Sam 6:18). The words of the blessing that Solomon said are not recorded, and perhaps they resemble what the high priest says (Num 6:22-27). The people needed to be reassured by this blessing in the face of the awe of God's indwelling and the fear of Him.
Solomon refers to the divine promise to David to build the house (2 Sam 7), praising the Lord, who promised first with His mouth, and then fulfilled with His hand what He had previously promised.

Solomon said, speaking of the mouth of the Lord, that the Lord had not specified for the people, since He brought them out of Egypt, any particular city among the cities of the tribes of Israel in which to build a house in the name of the Lord, but chose David as king over His people. Solomon had heard these words from his father, to whom Nathan the prophet had made them known (2 Sam 7). And it was David who thought of building the house, as Nathan the prophet told (2 Sam 7). God was dwelling in the midst of His people, in the tabernacle of meeting, which moved from place to place among the tribes, until God permitted a permanent house to be built for Him.

When God saw David's desire to build a house for Him, and then Solomon's carrying it out, He rejoiced, and came to dwell in the Temple and blessed it. And when God sees your longing and your striving toward Him through prayer and reading, He rejoices and blesses your life with many blessings beyond what you hope for.

God rejoiced at David's desire to build a house for God, but because David was occupied with many wars, to enlarge the kingdom and establish it, it was not fitting for him to build this great house, so He postponed this work to the days of his son Solomon, in whose reign there was stability and prosperity.

Solomon adds, saying: the Lord fulfilled what He promised, so I, his son, took over the throne, and I built the house in the name of the Lord, and I prepared a place for the ark, which holds the covenant of the Lord that He made with our fathers when He brought them out of Egypt, that is, the two tablets of the Law on which the commandments are written.
We notice in Solomon's words that he did not refer to the grandeur of the buildings of the house of God, or to the gold in it, but focused on two matters, namely:
1- God's promise to build a house for Him by the hand of the son of David.
2- The presence of the ark of God's covenant in the Temple.
That is, the greatness of the Temple rests on God's promise and His presence through the ark, and this is the secret of the Temple's strength, which is the image of heaven on earth.
(3) Praise of God and the covenant with Him (vv. 22-27)
22- And Solomon stood before the altar of the LORD in the presence of all the congregation of Israel, and spread forth his hands toward heaven:

23- And he said, LORD God of Israel, there is no God like thee, in heaven above, or on earth beneath, who keepest covenant and mercy with thy servants that walk before thee with all their heart: 24- Who hast kept with thy servant David my father that thou promisedst him: thou spakest also with thy mouth, and hast fulfilled it with thine hand, as it is this day. 25- Therefore now, LORD God of Israel, keep with thy servant David my father that thou promisedst him, saying, There shall not fail thee a man in my sight to sit on the throne of Israel; so that thy children take heed to their way, that they walk before me as thou hast walked before me. 26- And now, O God of Israel, let thy word, I pray thee, be verified, which thou spakest unto thy servant David my father. 27- But will God indeed dwell on the earth? behold, the heaven and heaven of heavens cannot contain thee; how much less this house that I have builded?
The altar of the Lord: what is meant is the bronze altar, before which a platform was set up for Solomon, and all the people stood behind him.

Solomon turned his face toward the altar of the Lord, leading all the people in their supplication to God, and lifted his hands toward heaven to praise the Lord. This shows Solomon's godliness and his understanding of the holy worship offered to God. And spreading out the hands means:
1- Showing one's need of God.
2- Presenting requests and needs to God, who is able to answer them.
3- Showing humility and reverence in supplicating to God.
4- Proclaiming faith in God's dwelling in heaven, that is, His being exalted above the thoughts of men.
5- Praising God and glorifying Him for His mercies and gifts.
The believers still lift up their hands to God in their prayers, whether the common prayers in the Church or the private prayers in their homes.

And Solomon, in this intercessory prayer for his people, is a type of Christ the Intercessor for His people (Jn 17). Solomon stood before the altar because his prayer rests on the sacrifice, which signifies the sacrifice of Christ; for by Christ our Redeemer we have access and boldness before the Father.

Through his praise, Solomon acknowledges that God has no likeness and no equal, neither in heaven nor on earth; He is the maker of mercy by fulfilling the divine promises, and He is a faithful God who keeps the covenant and kindness for those who love Him and keep His commandments, who walk in His ways uprightly. He is steadfast in keeping His promises despite the weakness of men and their failure to keep their promises toward Him, and then His mercy covers and completes every weakness in men; by His keeping of His promises and by His mercy, He receives His children despite their weakness.

God is true in His promises, and He had promised David to permit a house to be built for Him, and now by the power of God the divine promise has been fulfilled, and the house has been built by the hand of David's son, that is, Solomon the prophet.

Now Solomon asks the Lord to continue the kingship over the children of Israel for the house of David, as He promised him, saying that there would always be one of his offspring sitting on the throne of the kingdom, on condition that they keep the commandments and are faithful and upright (2 Sam 7:4-17). And God fulfilled His promise to the offspring of David: after the kingdom was divided, He left two tribes for the offspring of David to reign over, and this is the kingdom of Judah; then the greatest fulfillment of this promise came when Christ came from the offspring of David to reign over the hearts of those who believe in Him forever.
With his spiritual wisdom, Solomon realized that God, who fills every place, had condescended and was pleased to dwell in a specific place in the midst of His people.

May you glorify God in your prayers and praise Him, so that you may feel His greatness, and so stand in reverence before Him and receive His blessings, and ask of Him with confidence everything you want, for He is the Great One, who is able to do all things.
(4) Solomon's petitions (vv. 28-53)

28- Yet have thou respect unto the prayer of thy servant, and to his supplication, O LORD my God, to hearken unto the cry and to the prayer, which thy servant prayeth before thee to day: 29- That thine eyes may be open toward this house night and day, even toward the place of which thou hast said, My name shall be there: that thou mayest hearken unto the prayer which thy servant shall make toward this place. 30- And hearken thou to the supplication of thy servant, and of thy people Israel, when they shall pray toward this place: and hear thou in heaven thy dwelling place: and when thou hearest, forgive. 31- If any man trespass against his neighbour, and an oath be laid upon him to cause him to swear, and the oath come before thine altar in this house: 32- Then hear thou in heaven, and do, and judge thy servants, condemning the wicked, to bring his way upon his head; and justifying the righteous, to give him according to his righteousness. 33- When thy people Israel be smitten down before the enemy, because they have sinned against thee, and shall turn again to thee, and confess thy name, and pray, and make supplication unto thee in this house: 34- Then hear thou in heaven, and forgive the sin of thy people Israel, and bring them again unto the land which thou gavest unto their fathers. 35- When heaven is shut up, and there is no rain, because they have sinned against thee; if they pray toward this place, and confess thy name, and turn from their sin, when thou afflictest them: 36- Then hear thou in heaven, and forgive the sin of thy servants, and of thy people Israel, that thou teach them the good way wherein they should walk, and give rain upon thy land, which thou hast given to thy people for an inheritance.

37- If there be in the land famine, if there be pestilence, blasting, mildew, locust, or if there be caterpillar; if their enemy besiege them in the land of their cities; whatsoever plague, whatsoever sickness there be; 38- What prayer and supplication soever be made by any man, or by all thy people Israel, which shall know every man the plague of his own heart, and spread forth his hands toward this house:

39- Then hear thou in heaven thy dwelling place, and forgive, and do, and give to every man according to his ways, whose heart thou knowest; (for thou, even thou only, knowest the hearts of all the children of men;) 40- That they may fear thee all the days that they live in the land which thou gavest unto our fathers. 41- Moreover concerning a stranger, that is not of thy people Israel, but cometh out of a far country for thy name's sake; 42- (For they shall hear of thy great name, and of thy strong hand, and of thy stretched out arm;) when he shall come and pray toward this house; 43- Hear thou in heaven thy dwelling place, and do according to all that the stranger calleth to thee for: that all people of the earth may know thy name, to fear thee, as do thy people Israel; and that they may know that this house, which I have builded, is called by thy name. 44- If thy people go out to battle against their enemy, whithersoever thou shalt send them, and shall pray unto the LORD toward the city which thou hast chosen, and toward the house that I have built for thy name: 45- Then hear thou in heaven their prayer and their supplication, and maintain their cause. 46- If they sin against thee, (for there is no man that sinneth not,) and thou be angry with them, and deliver them to the enemy, so that they carry them away captives unto the land of the enemy, far or near; 47- Yet if they shall bethink themselves in the land whither they were carried captives, and repent, and make supplication unto thee in the land of them that carried them captives, saying, We have sinned, and have done perversely, we have committed wickedness; 48- And so return unto thee with all their heart, and with all their soul, in the land of their enemies, which led them away captive, and pray unto thee toward their land, which thou gavest unto their fathers, the city which thou hast chosen, and the house which I have built for thy name: 49- Then hear thou their prayer and their supplication in heaven thy dwelling place, and maintain their cause, 50- And forgive thy people that have sinned against thee, and all their transgressions wherein they have transgressed against thee, and give them compassion before them who carried them captive, that they may have compassion on them: 51- For they be thy people, and thine inheritance, which thou broughtest forth out of Egypt, from the midst of the furnace of iron:

52- That thine eyes may be open unto the supplication of thy servant, and unto the supplication of thy people Israel, to hearken unto them in all that they call for unto thee. 53- For thou didst separate them from among all the people of the earth, to be thine inheritance, as thou spakest by the hand of Moses thy servant, when thou broughtest our fathers out of Egypt, O Lord GOD.

Solomon asks the Lord to answer his supplications and prayers that he lifts up to the Lord on this day, and this shows the extent of Solomon's humility and reverence before God, and his sense of the greatness of His presence and also of his own intense need, so he cried out from the depth of his heart, asking for His help.
In this place: he means before the house of God.

Solomon asked God for His constant care and concern for His Temple and for all the petitions offered in it by Solomon and all the people of God, because the name of God has been called upon this place, and God in His love hears from heaven and forgives His people who cry out to Him that He may have mercy on them.
Laid an oath upon him: the person who suffered harm asked the person suspected to swear, in order to confirm his words.

If harm befalls a person, and he suspects another of being the cause of the harm that befell him, he brings him to the house of the Lord and has the suspected one swear, and let the Lord be the judge between them: if he swears falsely, the Lord condemns him, and if truly, the Lord justifies him. That is, Solomon asks God to be a judge for His people, so that He blesses the innocent and punishes the guilty, against whom no tangible evidence of guilt has appeared, for God is the searcher of hearts and minds, and thus all injustice is removed and God carries out His justice, punishing the wrongdoer and justifying the innocent.

God promised His people that He would keep them if they kept His commandments (Lev 26:1-13), but if they broke and transgressed them, they would be exposed to the attacks of their enemies and be defeated before them (Lev 26:14-39), and after their defeat, if they felt their sins and offered repentance before God toward His holy Temple, Solomon pleads with God to forgive them and bring them back by His power to their land from which the enemies had driven them out, and this is what happened in the captivity.

So that you may enjoy God's blessings that He has given you, may you keep His commandments and thank Him at all times, and not despise His long-suffering by persisting in committing sin, lest you lose these blessings.

If You withhold from Your people the rain that waters the crops because they sinned against You, and then they realized their error and acknowledged their iniquity and turned from their evil ways because they knew that You were disciplining them for their disobedience, then accept their repentance and answer their supplications and forgive them, and allow the sky to rain and water the land that You gave to Your people to dwell in. This actually happened in the days of Elijah the prophet, when the people left God and were immersed in the worship of Baal, but when they repented, God sent down rain after three years and six months.
Blasting: a hot wind that dries up plants and kills them.
Mildew: a plague that strikes crops and destroys them.
Caterpillar: locusts in the early stages of their growth, which multiply by the millions and are voracious, for it is the most dangerous stage of the growth of locusts.

If a famine occurs, or some pestilence spreads, or a scorching wind blows and strikes the crops, or locusts and plagues attack it, or if enemies besiege the cities of Your people, or if a disaster befalls Your people, then when any individual of all Your people prays or supplicates, aware of the transgression he has committed, and spreads out his hands toward this Temple, then answer from heaven, the place of Your dwelling, and pardon, and repay each one according to his ways; for You alone know what goes on in the mind of every man and You know the secrets of hearts, so You forgive the repentant who supplicate You and punish the wicked who persist in their sins.
When Your people see Your authority, O God, and Your forgiveness of the repentant and Your repayment of the wicked, they fear You and keep Your commandments.

Solomon gives an opportunity to the foreigners, that is, non-Jews, to enjoy praying before the house of God, so he asks Him to answer their petition if they come to Him because they heard of His power, and when He answers them they believe in Him and in His Temple, because of His superiority over their idols, and so they become proclaimers of God's power among the nations. Moses had permitted foreigners who love the people of God to dwell beside them and offer sacrifices to God (Num 15:14). These verses show God's love for the Jews and the Gentiles, which was completed in the fullness of time when Christ died for the salvation of all mankind.

If Your people go out to meet an enemy in any place You send them to, that is, a war by the command of the Lord and not from personal motives, and they pray to You, turning their faces toward the city You have chosen and the Temple You have built for Your name, then answer from heaven their prayers and their supplications, and give them victory over their enemies. Whenever they sought God before the war and He sent them to fight the enemies, they were victorious, but when they neglected to seek God they were defeated.
Maintain their cause: and rescue them and bring them back to their land.

If Your people sin and You permit, O God, their enemies to carry them captive to their own land, and Your people pray toward Your Temple and ask for Your help, then rescue them from the hands of their enemies and bring them back to their land. This actually happened in the Babylonian captivity, and God brought them back by the hand of Cyrus the Persian king (Ezra 7:12, 13).
From the midst of the furnace of iron: from the midst of a furnace for smelting iron, and it means hardships and torments.

If You permit, O God, Your people to remain for a period in captivity and they supplicate toward Your Temple, then forgive them and make those who carried them captive treat them gently, and shepherd them with Your mercy; for they are Your people whom You rescued from the slavery of Egypt and its torments.

May You always be attentive to my supplications to You and likewise the supplications of Your people, and may You answer all their petitions and their cries to You, for You chose them as Your children from among all the peoples, as You said by the tongue of Your servant Moses when You brought our fathers out of Egypt (Deut 4:20). We notice that Solomon focused on the petitions and needs of his people and not on his own petitions and needs, for he represents the faithful servant who cares for those he serves before himself.
And we see that Solomon in his prayer relies on God's Law that Moses received, for he holds fast to what the fathers lived by and what God taught them.

And the Book of Chronicles (2 Chr 7:1-3) tells us of God's pleasure with this prayer, for fire came down from heaven and consumed the sacrifices, and the glory of the Lord filled the house, so that the priests could not enter, and all bowed down before the great God who loves His people.

God is compassionate: whatever your sins may be, and even if you have been exposed to many problems because of them, He is ready to forgive you and remove all afflictions from you, indeed He honors you and glorifies you because you are His child.
(5) The closing blessing (vv. 54-61)

54- And it was so, that when Solomon had made an end of praying all this prayer and supplication unto the LORD, he arose from before the altar of the LORD, from kneeling on his knees with his hands spread up to heaven. 55- And he stood, and blessed all the congregation of Israel with a loud voice, saying, 56- Blessed be the LORD, that hath given rest unto his people Israel, according to all that he promised: there hath not failed one word of all his good promise, which he promised by the hand of Moses his servant.

57- The LORD our God be with us, as he was with our fathers: let him not leave us, nor forsake us: 58- That he may incline our hearts unto him, to walk in all his ways, and to keep his commandments, and his statutes, and his judgments, which he commanded our fathers. 59- And let these my words, wherewith I have made supplication before the LORD, be nigh unto the LORD our God day and night, that he maintain the cause of his servant, and the cause of his people Israel at all times, as the matter shall require: 60- That all the people of the earth may know that the LORD is God, and that there is none else.
61- Let your heart therefore be perfect with the LORD our God, to walk in his statutes, and to keep his commandments, as at this day.

Solomon prayed before the altar of the Lord, bowing on his knees, spreading his hands toward heaven, and then turned toward the people to bless them with a loud voice, and this closing blessing is a summary of Solomon's long prayer before it.
Blessed be the LORD: that is, He is worthy of glory and exaltation from His people.

Solomon prayed to God and glorified Him, because He gave His people a land to dwell in and find rest from those who troubled them, for He brought them out of the land of Egypt and kept them in the wilderness of Sinai and brought them into the land of Canaan and kept them in the days of the judges and raised up for them a good king, David, and after him his son Solomon, and thus He fulfilled all His good promises that He spoke by the tongue of His servant Moses.

Solomon asked God to remain with him and his people as He was with the fathers from the days of Abraham, and not be angry with them or withdraw from them, and to help them, so that their hearts might cling to Him, and they might live by His commandments and worship Him faithfully as the fathers lived with Him.

Solomon also pleaded with God to accept his prayers and the prayers of all his people, which they lift up to Him every day, by day and by night, and to care for them and supply all their needs and order all their affairs, and when the nations see what the Lord has done with them, they will acknowledge that the Lord, the God of Israel, is God and there is no other god besides Him.

Here Solomon addresses the people, asking of them complete devotion to the Lord and sincere loyalty to Him by walking according to His statutes and obeying His commandments, as they did today, that is, the day of the dedication of the Temple, when they were in spiritual zeal and readiness to obey the commandments of God.

May you be steadfast in your relationship with God; when you promise Him that you will live with Him and commit to a specific striving, take care to follow up on these promises so that they do not grow lukewarm and weak. Be careful to renew your promises every day before God, and so enjoy fellowship with Him and rejoice in His care for you.
(6) Offering sacrifices and celebrations (vv. 62-66)

62- And the king, and all Israel with him, offered sacrifice before the LORD. 63- And Solomon offered a sacrifice of peace offerings, which he offered unto the LORD, two and twenty thousand oxen, and an hundred and twenty thousand sheep. So the king and all the children of Israel dedicated the house of the LORD. 64- The same day did the king hallow the middle of the court that was before the house of the LORD: for there he offered burnt offerings, and meat offerings, and the fat of the peace offerings: because the brasen altar that was before the LORD was too little to receive the burnt offerings, and meat offerings, and the fat of the peace offerings. 65- And at that time Solomon held a feast, and all Israel with him, a great congregation, from the entering in of Hamath unto the river of Egypt, before the LORD our God, seven days and seven days, even fourteen days. 66- On the eighth day he sent the people away: and they blessed the king, and went unto their tents joyful and glad of heart for all the goodness that the LORD had done for David his servant, and for Israel his people.

After Solomon's prayer, he offered with his people many sacrifices to God, most of them perhaps peace offerings, which signify thanks to God for what He had done with them, in permitting a house to be built for Him in their midst. And perhaps they offered some sin offerings, that God might forgive them their sins; and likewise some burnt offerings, which signify their readiness to consecrate their hearts to God.

The peace offerings that were sacrificed during the period of the celebrations were enormous in number: 22 thousand oxen and 120 thousand sheep. Thus the king and all the people dedicated the house of the Lord.

Dedication means consecrating the holy place and beginning to use it and to enjoy worship in it. We notice that the dedication is carried out by prayer and the offering of sacrifices, and this signifies that the consecration of holy places is carried out by the sacrifice of Christ the Savior and by prayer to Him, for without shedding of blood there is no remission (Heb 9:22). The many sacrifices proclaim:
1- The great love of Solomon and his people for God.
2- Their sense of God's greatness and His condescension in having a permanent dwelling in their midst.
3- The wealth of Solomon and his people.
4- Their deep thanks to God for His good pleasure to dwell in a permanent Temple in their midst.
5- Their making a covenant with God by eating of the sacrifices, that they might live for Him.
6- Their acknowledgment of their weakness and sins and their need of God's mercy.

These sacrifices were probably not offered in one day but throughout the fourteen days in which the celebrations of the dedication of the Temple continued (v. 65). Most of these sacrifices were probably from Solomon's own money, and the rest from the offerings of the people and their leaders.

As for the peace offerings, a part of them was offered to God, the second part was taken by the priests, and the third part that remained was eaten by those who offered the sacrifices, with care to include the Levites, the poor and everyone in need in eating of these sacrifices (Lev 7:11); that is, they offered sacrifices to God, and He gave them of them, and they ate from the hand of God and rejoiced. This shows that the days of the dedication of the Temple were days of very great joy and gladness for all the people.

The offering of the sacrifices was accompanied by the sounding of trumpets, the playing of instruments of song and continuous praise of God, most likely by chanting the psalms that glorify God (2 Chr 7:6). And when the Scripture says that Solomon sacrificed these huge numbers, it is implicitly understood that he did not sacrifice them himself, because he is not a priest. The number of the priests was very large, about three thousand, and the Levites who assisted them numbered about 40 thousand. And these sacrifices were carried out, as we said, over a period of 14 days, and therefore it was possible to offer these huge numbers.

Solomon made a large bronze altar on which to offer the fat of the sacrifices as the Law prescribes, but no altar, however large, could hold the huge numbers that were offered at the dedication of the Temple. Therefore Solomon was compelled to consecrate a large area at the entrance of the house of the Lord, around the bronze altar, for offering the sacrifices on it, and perhaps he set up temporary altars for this occasion and put on them some of the holy fire that was on the bronze altar (Ex 40). The animal sacrifices, as well as the offerings of flour and other grain offerings, were offered on these altars.
Hamath: a Syrian city at a distance of 200 km north of Damascus.

The river of Egypt: or the brook of Egypt in some translations, it is the Wadi el-Arish, the last southern boundary of the tribe of Judah, and it is a seasonal stream that fills with water in winter and dries up in summer, and it marks the border between Egypt and the land of the children of Israel.

The people of God gathered from the farthest part of the land in the north, that is, from the entrance of Hamath, to its farthest part in the south, which is the river of Egypt; all of them came to Jerusalem to rejoice at the dedication of the Temple, and kept a feast for seven days for this purpose, and this was in the seventh month, before the feast of Tabernacles, which begins on the fifteenth day of it. So after the seven days in which they celebrated the dedication, they continued for another seven days to celebrate the feast of Tabernacles, in which the Law requires all the males of the children of Israel to come to Jerusalem to stand before the house of God. It was a good choice on Solomon's part to choose the occasion of the feast of Tabernacles, in which the people gather from every place, and to place the dedication of the Temple in the seven days before it (Lev 23).

The eighth day of the feast of Tabernacles, which is the twenty-first day of the seventh month, is a day of solemn rest, as the Law prescribes, and no work is done in it except prayer and worship (Lev 23:33-36). So after the end of this day Solomon blessed the people, after they had enjoyed the worship of God, and the people responded to him and blessed him; that is, they prayed for blessing for him on account of his care in building the house of the Lord. And here we see the great love between the king and his people and their being bound together in the love of God and the worship of Him, so God covered them with His care and blessing. Then they departed rejoicing and returned to their homes glorifying God.

How beautiful it is for you to offer prayers for those around you and encourage them with kind words, for this rejoices the heart of God and rejoices others, and then your own heart rejoices too, especially since others will often pray for you and ask blessing for you, so you live as though you were in heaven.
God's appearance to Solomon, his constructions and his trade

God appeared to Solomon after he sat on the throne of Israel, at Gibeon, when he offered sacrifices to God (ch. 3) and asked Him to give him wisdom. Now He appears to him a second time, thirteen years after the dedication of the Temple, to declare to Solomon His joy in what he had accomplished and to warn him against being immersed in wealth and the desires of the world, lest he go astray. For he had completed the building of his palaces and had begun to be occupied with the many marriages to foreign women. Here the love of God, His wisdom and His care for His children appear, for He encourages them and warns them against sin before they fall into it.

We do not know in what form God's appearance took place, whether a dream or a vision or some other form, such as his hearing a voice or the appearing of a mist or the like, but Solomon was certain that God was speaking to him. Of course he did not see the essence of God, because "No man hath seen God at any time" (Jn 1:18).

The Lord told Solomon that his prayer had risen before Him, and here He answers his petitions and declares His good pleasure with what he had done. For when Solomon completed the building of the Temple, his work stopped at that point, but the sanctification of the house is the work of God Himself, declaring His acceptance of this gift. And God, as He declares His presence in the house, reveals what He has decided, namely that from now on He will set His eye, that is, His care, and His heart, that is, His love, upon this house; for God cares for His Temple and for all the acts of worship offered in it. God's care for Solomon's Temple does not mean that it would not be exposed to destruction, as the Jews thought, because He said "for ever," but God keeps His Temple as long as His people are subject to Him and keep His commandments; but when they were occupied away from Him with the worship of idols and evil desires, He refused to dwell among them, and permitted the Temple to be burned by the hand of Babylon (2 Kgs 24), and then by the hand of the Romans. What is meant by His care for His Temple forever is His presence in His Church, which extends forever in the Kingdom of Heaven.

Here the Lord confirms His promise, conditional upon the continuance of the kingship for the offspring of David, as He had promised his father before, and the condition was perseverance in keeping the commandments with uprightness of heart, as David did.

And this is a positive condition, in addition to negative conditions that He will mention in the following verses. The continuation of Solomon's offspring on his throne forever means Christ, who comes from his offspring and reigns forever in the Kingdom of Heaven.

And God's warning to Solomon to keep His commandments means that he should not be occupied with the love of women and foreign wives, or with the acquiring of gold and the multiplying of horses and various possessions, lest they distract him from God, for the goal of his life is to worship God faithfully.

But if the people of God in any generation turn aside from the way of the Lord and His commandments and worship idols, like the nations, then God warns them that He will cast them out of the land that He had given them, and He will neglect the house that He sanctified, so that it will be exposed to ruin, and Israel will become a proverb and a byword among all the peoples around them.

Despite the clarity of God's words that He could permit His Temple to be destroyed, the Jews continued to believe that the Temple would remain forever, although it was destroyed by the hand of Babylon, and then by the hand of the Romans after the Resurrection of Christ (Lk 19:44). And the Jews still think that they will build the Temple, and they do not want to understand the spiritual meaning, which is faith in Christ and submission to Him, so that He reigns over their hearts in His Church forever.
Hiss: a declaration of astonishment and mockery.

The Temple, which was a place of pride and honor for the children of Israel, will become an astonishment to everyone who passes by it, who will be amazed at its ruin and ask why the Lord has done so to this land and to this Temple. This was accomplished in 586 BC, when the Temple was destroyed and burned in the Babylonian captivity.

The answer to their question will come to them thus: because they forsook the Lord their God, who saved their fathers from Egypt, the house of bondage, and brought them out of it, and they turned aside after other gods, bowed down to them and worshiped them, so all this evil came upon them. And this divine warning is a clear prophecy of the destruction of the Temple.

Your way with God, by keeping His commandments, guarantees you rest and joy. So why do you go away from Him, and even provoke Him with your sins and persist in them, and so lose everything? The way of God is always open to you through repentance, so do not neglect it.

The building of the Temple took seven years, and the building of Solomon's palace and its annexes took another thirteen years, so the total time those constructions required was twenty years. Solomon built the buildings in this order:
1- The house of the Lord, which is the most important place because it is the place of worship and of meeting with God.
2- Solomon's house, which represents the royal stability and the administration of the kingdom.
3- The house of Pharaoh's daughter, which provides for family stability.
4- The storehouses and the stables for the horses, which arrange the economic needs.

We see from the above that Solomon followed the right order in his constructions: the house of the Lord is more important than his own house, and family stability and the administration of the kingdom are more important than the economic matters.

May you set the priorities of your life in order, for time is not enough for everything, and therefore your attention to some matters before others, because of their importance, gives you stability. And do not forget, in the press of life, to give priority to your relationship with God and your service.
Helped: aided him, that is, helped him quickly.

Hiram king of Tyre took care to help Solomon in his many constructions, and Solomon paid him large quantities of wheat, oil and foodstuffs (ch. 5), and Solomon also wanted to complete the rewarding of Hiram for his cooperation with him, but the treasury of the kingdom had run low of money because of Solomon's spending much gold on building palaces and on the many marriages and on acquiring horses, and this is the opposite of what the Law commanded (Deut 17:16, 17). And because of these many costs Solomon was forced to give up 20 cities belonging to the tribes of Naphtali and Zebulun, which he had taken, and other cities of the nations, to enlarge his kingdom and fulfill God's promise that the kingdom of Israel would extend from the Euphrates to the river of Egypt; that is, God helped him enlarge his kingdom, but he gave up part of the land that God had given him, and this was of course a mistake on his part, for the Jews held fast to the land and regarded it as a gift from God and an inheritance from the fathers that they could not give up, and so the Law commanded (Lev 25:23). This region, which includes the twenty cities and what is around them, was called Galilee of the Gentiles, because the Gentiles lived in it with the Jews (Isa 9:1, Mt 4:15), and this encouraged idol worship in it, and then idol worship spread through all the land of the people of God, until Christ came and preached in Galilee and drew them to the right faith.

Cabul: a mountainous district in Galilee, located southeast of Acre at a distance of ten miles, and its name also means boundary, because it was outside the boundaries of the lands of the children of Israel. Hiram went to inspect those cities, and he did not like them, because their land is mountainous and he prefers cities in the valleys, or on trade routes, or beside the sea, because his main work is trade; so he apologized to Solomon for not accepting these cities, especially since they were friends and brothers and Solomon would not be upset with him.
A talent of gold: equals 3000 shekels of gold, and a shekel of gold equals 11-15 g.

Hiram sensed the weakness of the financial situation and the scarcity of gold in Solomon's treasuries, so out of the love between them he sent Solomon a gift of 120 talents of gold, and Solomon thanked him, and because of Solomon's faithfulness he considered it a loan that he repaid to Hiram, when he made him a partner in the trade in the ships that Solomon owned, which returned a large financial profit to Hiram (v. 27).

entries.section: (3) Solomon's constructions and his forced labor of the Gentiles

paragraphs.text: Millo: it is the fortress of Zion or the city of David (2 Chr 32:5). Hazor: it was the capital of the kingdom of the Canaanites in northern Palestine (Josh 11); the children of Israel and the Canaanites exchanged control over it, and when Solomon took it he fortified it, and then Tiglath-pileser took it when the kingdom of Assyria attacked Israel (2 Kgs 15:29). Megiddo: it is the one called "Armageddon," that is, the hill of Megiddo, in the Book of Revelation (Rev 16:16). A city of Manasseh located southeast of Haifa by about 32 km, in which there were stables for Solomon's horses.
Gezer: an ancient Canaanite city about 30 km west of Jerusalem.

Because of the many constructions he undertook, Solomon needed to impose a system of forced labor. The building works he carried out were the Temple and then his palace, and he also renewed the city of David and its walls after they had fallen into ruin with the passing of time, and he built citadels, fortresses and important sites, such as Hazor, Megiddo and Gezer.

entries.section: (3) Solomon's constructions and his forced labor of the Gentiles

paragraphs.text: The children of Israel took Gezer when they entered the land of Canaan, but the Philistines were able to recover it from the children of Israel, and then Gezer began to attack Egypt, so Pharaoh attacked it and took it and burned it and killed those in it, and gave it as a gift to his daughter, as a dowry for her marriage to Solomon, as kings used to do in the past.

entries.section: (3) Solomon's constructions and his forced labor of the Gentiles

paragraphs.text: Nether Beth-horon: a village 20 km north of Jerusalem, built on low ground, and it is one of the cities that David fortified.

Baalath: also called "Baalah of Judah" or "Kirjath-baal" or "Kirjath-jearim," where the ark remained for a time, and it is one of the cities of the tribe of Dan (Josh 19:44). It is 15 km west of Jerusalem.

Tadmor: it was one of the most beautiful cities of the world, which Solomon fortified to control the routes of the caravans passing through it. It is located 140 miles northeast of Damascus and 120 miles west of the river Euphrates.
The wilderness: the desert surrounding the city.
The land: the places that Solomon took and that became part of his kingdom.
Solomon rebuilt Gezer and also set up many constructions in cities with important locations, namely Nether Beth-horon, and Baalath and Tadmor in the desert lands.

entries.section: (3) Solomon's constructions and his forced labor of the Gentiles

paragraphs.text: That which Solomon desired: that is, the buildings and gardens that he made for his recreation.

He also built the cities that had storehouses for agricultural produce and building materials, and the cities that had storehouses for the war chariots and dwellings for the horsemen to live in, for the number of his chariots was large, so he needed several cities in which to put them (ch. 10:26). Thus Solomon made all the structures that he desired, in Jerusalem and in Lebanon and in all parts of his kingdom, so it was difficult to count all the constructions he made because of their multitude.

entries.section: (3) Solomon's constructions and his forced labor of the Gentiles

paragraphs.text: The Amorites: a people who ruled parts of Palestine and Syria for some time; their line of descent goes back to Canaan, and they remained in the land of Canaan after the Hebrews conquered it.
The Hittites: they are the origin of the present-day Armenians and are not Semites. They came to Asia Minor early, and Solomon had Hittite women among his wives.
The Perizzites: an important branch of the Canaanite branches who were not wiped out when the children of Israel entered the Promised Land. The Hivites: they are one of the races of the Canaanites.

The Jebusites: a Canaanite tribe that lived in "Jebus," which is Jerusalem, and they lived with the children of Judah and Benjamin and continued to hold the fortress of Zion until the days of David, who took their fortress and made it part of Jerusalem, his capital. Some of them remained in the city after David took it, and their presence in the city continued until after the return from the Babylonian captivity.

To set up his many structures Solomon needed many laborers, so he used the descendants of the peoples who remained in the Promised Land because the children of Israel were not able to wipe them out: the Amorites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Hivites and the Jebusites, who were not of the children of Israel, and Solomon imposed on them forced labor as slaves.

entries.section: (3) Solomon's constructions and his forced labor of the Gentiles

paragraphs.text: Captains: plural of third, which is an advanced military rank: the king is first, the princes are in second place, and then these thirds. They used to ride in the king's own chariot, since each chariot carried three persons.

As for the children of Israel, Solomon did not subject any of them to forced labor, but made them soldiers and officers, commanders of chariots and horsemen, and among them were the men of his court and his princes.

entries.section: (3) Solomon's constructions and his forced labor of the Gentiles

paragraphs.text: The number of those who supervised the workers subjected to forced labor for building was 550 men.

God blessed Solomon and helped him take many lands to enlarge his kingdom and set up structures for all the needs of the kingdom. God is ready to bless you and everything you do if you submit to His commandments and walk uprightly before Him. So seek God before everything, and He will arrange all your affairs for you.

After Pharaoh's daughter moved from the city of David to her palace that Solomon built for her west of the Temple, he built Millo, which is the fortress of Zion, or the city of David, which was mentioned before in (v. 15). And the Book of Chronicles tells us in (2 Chr 8:11) of the reason for which Solomon changed the dwelling of Pharaoh's daughter, for he said, "My wife shall not dwell in the house of David king of Israel, because the places are holy, whereunto the ark of the LORD hath come" (2 Chr 8:11). The ark had earlier come to rest in the city of David (2 Sam 6:12), in the very house of King David, and then Solomon carried it from the city of David, or Zion, to the Temple, so it was not possible for the Gentile wife to dwell in the place that had been sanctified by the presence of the ark of God's covenant.

Solomon kept on offering burnt offerings and peace offerings on the bronze altar that he built for the Lord, and he also burned incense on the golden altar by means of the priests three times a year, at the feasts of Passover, Pentecost and Tabernacles, as the Lord's commandment to them. This shows the extent of Solomon's attachment to the worship of God and his personal need of God's blessing in his life.

Do not forget, in the press of life, whatever your responsibilities, your need for prayer and for attending church and enjoying the Holy Sacraments, for they are your food and your strength, and by this God dwells in you and you abide in His Church.

Ezion-geber: a city at the northern end of the Gulf of Aqaba near the port of Eilat. Solomon built his naval fleet there on the Red Sea, and thereby controlled trade with the Arabian Peninsula, India and the eastern coast of Africa.
Eloth: it is the present port of Eilat, and it is located east of Ezion-geber and beside it.
The Red Sea: it is the Red Sea.

Ophir: a region most likely in present-day Yemen, famous in ancient times for gold. Solomon and Hiram sent their joint fleet to it, which they built from the timber of Lebanon, to bring gold and precious stones.
King Solomon cared for trade besides his care for constructions, and he began to build a naval fleet at Ezion-geber, next to the present port of Eilat on the shore of the Red Sea.

A strong friendship and a treaty of brotherhood and cooperation bound Solomon to Hiram, so Hiram sent in the ships sailors of great experience in maritime work and the steering of ships, to accompany Solomon's men on their trading voyages and pass on their expertise to them.

Among the places to which Solomon sent his ships was the region of Ophir, and he bought from there 420 talents of gold, which is a very large quantity, equal to millions of pounds, and this shows Solomon's wealth. Solomon's wealth and the visit of the queen of Sheba to him

entries.section: (1) The visit of the queen of Sheba to Solomon

paragraphs.text: Sheba: an independent kingdom in the south of the Arabian Peninsula, which is present-day Yemen, but the Ethiopians consider that this queen was their queen and that she married Solomon and bore him a son whom she called Menelik, who was the father of the kings of Ethiopia, among them Candace, queen of Ethiopia (Acts 8:27). And Christ calls her the queen of Teman, that is, of the south (Lk 11:31), because her country lies south of the people of Israel. She is an example of the Gentiles who accepted the faith in the Old Testament (Lk 11:29, 32). Concerning the name of the LORD: that is, all of Solomon's wisdom and wealth is attributed to God.

The queen of Sheba heard much about Solomon, and about his wisdom, his knowledge and his wealth, and that he was a godly man of God, so she came herself to Jerusalem, not believing what she had heard about him, and she put questions to him to make sure of his wisdom. Perhaps they were questions in different fields, religious, administrative and scientific.
If you hold fast to God, He is glorified in you and you become a light to the world. So take care of your relationship with God, so that you may be a good image of Him and people may see God in you.

entries.section: (1) The visit of the queen of Sheba to Solomon

paragraphs.text: The queen of Sheba came to Jerusalem with a huge caravan of camels loaded with gifts of spices, much gold and precious stones, and she met King Solomon and laid her questions before him.

entries.section: (1) The visit of the queen of Sheba to Solomon

paragraphs.text: Solomon had the satisfying, convincing answer to all her inquiries, and he was not unable to answer any of the matters she put to him.

entries.section: (1) The visit of the queen of Sheba to Solomon

paragraphs.text: There was no more spirit in her: she was overwhelmed and greatly astonished.

When the queen of Sheba saw the greatness of Solomon's gifts and his wisdom in building the Temple and organizing the service in it, and the administrative arrangements surrounding it, from the officials of his palace and the beauty of their clothing, and his servants who were always present to serve him, and his keeping of the ordinances of his Law by offering the burnt offerings in the Temple, deep amazement and exceeding astonishment came over her.

If the queen of Sheba came to Solomon from far away to see his wisdom, are you concerned to come to the Church to see the power of Christ in His Sacraments and to lift up prayers before Him, so that you enjoy abundant blessings and are satisfied with His love?

entries.section: (1) The visit of the queen of Sheba to Solomon

paragraphs.text: Before what she saw with her own eyes, she could do no other than acknowledge before the king the truth of all she had heard about him and his wisdom while she was in her own country, before she came to Jerusalem.

entries.section: (1) The visit of the queen of Sheba to Solomon

paragraphs.text: She confessed to him that when she first heard the reports about him she doubted their truth because of their greatness, but when she came and saw and looked into matters herself, she realized that what she had heard did not amount to half of what she saw. Perhaps she also asked Solomon about the Lord when she found Solomon offering his sacrifices and his worship with great reverence, so she was moved and her heart began to accept faith in God.

entries.section: (1) The visit of the queen of Sheba to Solomon

paragraphs.text: The queen praised Solomon for his greatness, which his men who stand before him and his servants who serve him enjoy seeing, and she blessed the Lord his God, who loved him and set him on the throne of Israel, for it was out of the Lord's love for His people Israel that He set over them a wise king like him to lead them with wisdom and justice; and the queen of Sheba's blessing the Lord shows that she had begun to believe in Him.

entries.section: (1) The visit of the queen of Sheba to Solomon

paragraphs.text: The queen gave Solomon the gifts she had brought, which were 120 talents of gold, the same quantity that Hiram had given Solomon (ch. 9:14), and many spices and precious stones. The spice she brought and gave to King Solomon was very abundant, exceeding in quantity all the spice that had come to Solomon. Solomon here is a type of Christ, and the gifts of the queen of Sheba are a type of the gifts of the Magi.

entries.section: (1) The visit of the queen of Sheba to Solomon

paragraphs.text: Almug wood: one of the precious woods, and it has a sweet fragrance.

In addition to what the queen of Sheba presented, King Hiram's ships brought much gold from "Ophir," and also almug wood in great quantities and precious stones too. Solomon used the almug wood to make railings for the stairs of the house of the Lord and his palace, and he also made from it harps and psalteries for the singers. And there came no such almug trees, nor were seen, to the day of the writing of this book.

entries.section: (1) The visit of the queen of Sheba to Solomon

paragraphs.text: Solomon gave the queen of Sheba many gifts, including everything she asked of him, as a sign of friendship between their two countries, and added to it all that the generosity of kings bestows, and she turned and went back to her own country, she and her retinue.

If the queen of Sheba was greatly moved by Solomon's wisdom and arrangements and wealth, how much more are our hearts amazed when we contemplate the greatness of Christ and His wisdom and wealth and His infinite power, for He is able to give us everything and solve all our problems and protect us from every error.

The queen of Sheba came from the ends of the earth when she heard of Solomon's wisdom .. so what is our striving to know Christ and enjoy fellowship with Him? How great is the striving of our prayers and fasts and readings? What is the extent of our persistence and our seeking toward Him?
And the queen of Sheba presented many gifts to Solomon .. so what do we present to our Christ? Not material gifts only, but rather our hearts and our time.

The queen of Teman took care to ask Solomon many questions in order to benefit from his wisdom, and we who know the weakness of our understanding, do we seek Christ the Word, who is the source of wisdom for the whole world, and consult Him in all our works with many prayers?

entries.section: (2) The wealth and glory of Solomon

paragraphs.text: A talent of gold = about 34 kilograms.
The traffic of the merchants: the merchants used to pay gold to Solomon as customs and transit fees for the trade routes that he had set up.

The kings of Arabia and the governors of the country: what is meant is the countries that Solomon subdued and that surrounded his country, and they paid him tribute. The governors of the country may also mean the leaders of the children of Israel who paid taxes to Solomon.

The weight of the gold that Solomon obtained in one year was about 23 tons. This is apart from the much gold that the merchants of the countries subject to him presented to him, and likewise the kings and rulers of those lands, which was presented to him as tribute that they were obliged to pay periodically and regularly, so his annual income from it was beyond count. In addition, the abundance of trade and the residence of merchants in the land of the children of Israel brought the country much money, in return for their residence and their business, which increased the gold and prosperity in the country. But the six hundred sixty-six talents of gold were not an annual income; rather, in one of the years Solomon obtained this quantity.

This shows Solomon's excessive concern and love for money, and all this gold was carried off by Pharaoh Shishak, king of Egypt, five years after Solomon's death (ch. 14:25, 26; 2 Chr 9, 12:2-11). For godliness with contentment is great gain. So, my brother, do not be occupied with money, for it is passing away, and if you have money, thank God for it but do not cling to it, for security and happiness are from God.

entries.section: (2) The wealth and glory of Solomon

paragraphs.text: Target: a shield that the soldier carries to ward off arrows and spears from his chest.
Beaten gold: hammered gold, that is, shaped and worked by hammering.
(The shekel: 11-15 grams.) Shield: armor, a long guard that protects the soldier's body along its length.
Pounds: plural of mina, which is 100 shekels.

The target that the soldier carried to defend himself was made in that time of wood and covered with a layer of leather, but Solomon made two hundred targets of beaten gold, and the weight of the gold used in each target was 7 kg; he also made 300 shields of beaten gold, and the gold used in each shield was 3 kg. And he hung the targets and shields for adornment, as was the custom in ancient times, on the walls of the house of the forest of Lebanon, which he had built before.

Targets and shields are defensive means that the soldier uses, so they declare that Solomon defends the right and the oppressed, and is not like the Romans, whose procession was led by axes and rods, which represent violence and attack and the oppression of others.

entries.section: (2) The wealth and glory of Solomon

paragraphs.text: Best gold: pure gold.

Solomon made a magnificent throne, made of ivory and overlaid with pure gold, and one went up to the throne by six steps. The throne had a round top behind, and perhaps there was a canopy above the seat, with a support behind the seat in which were fixed two armrests on its sides around the place of sitting, and two lions standing beside the armrests. The two lions proclaim the power of God that was with Solomon, so that he fears no one and justice is carried out in his kingdom with all strength (see the picture of the judgment seat at the end of the book).

entries.section: (2) The wealth and glory of Solomon

paragraphs.text: Solomon set twelve lions on the six steps, six on each side, so the throne was more magnificent than any throne of the kings in that age. The twelve lions proclaim to the twelve tribes that they should trust in the power of God that is with them and walk in justice and strength and fear no one.

entries.section: (2) The wealth and glory of Solomon

paragraphs.text: The drinking vessels and all the other vessels that were in the king's palace and in the house of the forest of Lebanon were all made of pure gold, and none of them was made of silver, for silver had no value because of its abundance in the time in which Solomon reigned.

entries.section: (2) The wealth and glory of Solomon

paragraphs.text: Tarshish: it is Tartessus, located in the south of Spain near Gibraltar, and it was a city very rich in mineral wealth.

Apes and peacocks: they were among the costly things, and importing them represented luxury in Solomon's life. Solomon had a commercial naval fleet that he built in cooperation with King Hiram, and their ships sailed the seas and went to "Tarshish" and other coastal cities, and returned once every three years to their bases on the coasts of Israel carrying gold and silver and ivory and apes and peacocks, and unloaded their cargo there. Tarshish was considered the last country of the known ancient world before the discovery of the Americas, that is, Solomon's ships passed by all the important trading countries in the world. Thus Solomon's stature grew greater than all the kings of the earth, for he surpassed them all in wealth and wisdom.

entries.section: (2) The wealth and glory of Solomon

paragraphs.text: Delegations from all parts of the inhabited world used to come to the land of Israel seeking to see King Solomon and to hear his wisdom, which God had given him.
And Solomon's greatness surpassed that of the greatest countries of the world existing at that time, namely Egypt and Assyria.

Solomon used the wisdom he received in managing the affairs of government and carrying out great building works and reviving trade with all the peoples. May we too use the gifts that God has given us for the benefit of ourselves and others. Each of us God has endowed with many gifts, so let us use them in the service of our brethren and our Church, and not live for ourselves alone.

entries.section: (2) The wealth and glory of Solomon

paragraphs.text: The visitors who came did not come empty-handed, but came with gifts that varied among vessels of silver and gold, garments, weapons, spices, horses and mules, and the visits were repeated from year to year, and their bringing gifts yearly implied their submission to him, for it was regarded as tribute that they had to pay.

entries.section: (2) The wealth and glory of Solomon

paragraphs.text: Chariots: that is, war chariots and civil ones drawn by horses.

Solomon gathered chariots and horsemen, so he had 1400 chariots and 12 thousand horsemen, and Solomon distributed them among the storehouses that he had set up before in the chariot cities, and kept some of them in the capital of his kingdom, Jerusalem.

entries.section: (2) The wealth and glory of Solomon

paragraphs.text: Silver in Jerusalem was regarded as stones are regarded, in terms of its abundance and its being everywhere, that is, it had no value, just as the precious cedar wood, because of its plenty, became worth no more than the very cheap sycamore wood.

entries.section: (2) The wealth and glory of Solomon

paragraphs.text: Linen yarn (what was brought): that which is brought in, that is, imported, from other countries.
The Syrians: peoples living in different places, the most important of which is the region of present-day Syria.

Solomon used to import horses from Egypt, and the king's merchants obtained them at cheap prices because of Solomon's marriage to Pharaoh's daughter, so a war chariot was bought for about seven kg of silver and a horse for two kilograms of silver. The merchants used to re-export some of them to the kings of the Hittites and the Syrians, and so gained from the difference in price, and this is the meaning of his saying "they brought them out by their means."

Solomon's acquiring horses in abundance is contrary to the Law, for God commanded not to multiply them, so that man would not rely on his strength and would not be occupied with the world (Deut 16:17-20). Solomon's deviation and the Lord's punishment of him
Moabitesses and Ammonitesses: from the daughters of the peoples of Moab and the children of Ammon, who are the sons of Lot by his two daughters, and the two peoples lived east of the river Jordan.
Edomites: daughters of Edom, and Edom is Esau; his tribe lived east of the Gulf of Aqaba and south of the children of Israel.
Zidonians: daughters of Sidon, which is present-day "Saida," a famous Lebanese city on the coast of the Mediterranean.
Hittites: daughters of Heth, and it is probable that the sons of Heth are the origin of the present-day Armenians, and they lived north of the land of the Jews beside Hamath.

Solomon's heart was kindled with the love of women, and his desire led him to be joined to many wives, not only from the children of Israel but also from the peoples surrounding his country, such as the Moabitesses, the Ammonitesses, the Edomites, the Zidonians and the Hittites. What encouraged him in this was that in his days the greatness of the kings of the nations was measured by the multitude of their women, and perhaps he also intended political aims in strengthening his kingdom by being joined to the kings and leaders of these peoples.
But this was contrary to God's Law in the following respects:
1- The Law forbade multiplying marriages (Deut 17:16, 17).

2- The Law also forbade marrying foreign women, lest they turn the people of God away from worshiping Him, so that they would be bound to the gods of the pagan nations (Ex 34:15, 16, Deut 7:3), and this is what actually happened with Solomon.

Of course the multitude of marriages made the king's expenses very great, so that Solomon's wealth did not suffice for his expenses and the treasury of the kingdom was in need, which made him increase taxes and burden his people; so he wronged and oppressed his people for the sake of his many desires.

And we notice that when God blessed Solomon and gave him many good things and wisdom, he was occupied with his desires, whereas he ought to have cared for the worship of God and the teaching of his children and his people so as to raise them spiritually, but he was content with building the house of God and then became occupied with his palaces and his desires, so he began to move away from God.

So be careful, however great your intelligence and knowledge, lest you slip into the desires of the world, by holding fast to God's commandments and submitting to your spiritual father and examining yourself every day and humbling yourself before God, and He will rescue you from the snares of the devil.

When Solomon was joined to a thousand wives, his love for God began to weaken and he moved away from the fear of God. He thought that his happiness lay in these women, so he became infatuated with them and fell under their influence.

This number of women is astonishing, and if it shows us anything, it shows that if we are lax in holding fast to the words of God and the door is opened for man's decline, it is hard for him to stop at a certain limit. Let us beware of the beginning, which may be simple but drags behind it a flood of deviations.

Solomon was influenced by the many foreign marriages, so he began to humor his wives by setting up idols for their gods, and thus in his old age he worshiped idols alongside the worship of God, and his wisdom could not protect him, because he had moved away from God and did not live with uprightness of heart, like David his father, who refused idol worship completely throughout his life. Many of the Fathers see that Solomon repented at the end of his life and wrote the Book of Ecclesiastes, which shows his renunciation of all desires and his return to the worship of God alone.

And if we say that Solomon died at about sixty years of age, then the time of his old age would be about fifty, which is an early age, but it was considered old age for him because of his great absorption in bodily pleasures and the cares and weariness that resulted from them, which made him reach old age early.

Ashtoreth the goddess of the Zidonians: the chief goddess in both Babylon and Assyria and in the coastal cities of the Phoenicians; she was always worshiped with a male god, Baal; she and Baal were symbols of the moon and the sun.

Milcom the abomination of the Ammonites: Molech, the god of the Ammonites. Human sacrifices, especially of children, were offered to him, and his idol was made of hollow bronze, in whose cavity a fierce fire was lit, and the child was placed on the two very hot arms of the statue, while during that they beat drums to prevent his cries from being heard. Solomon allowed his Zidonian wives to worship their goddess Ashtoreth, as he allowed the Ammonite women to worship their gods Milcom, under the influence of their urging him to accept their gods. Although it is probable that he did not take part in this worship himself, but allowed it, and he may have loved it.

By this Solomon disobeyed the Lord his God and walked with other gods, and worshiped them along with the worship of the one true God, and this was evil in the sight of the Lord, who had warned him twice in two visions lest he fall into it.
Chemosh the abomination of the Moabites: the god of the Moabites. The manner of his worship was like the worship of "Molech," by offering children as sacrifices to him, and he is a sun god.

To please his wives he built a high place dedicated to the worship of the pagan god "Chemosh," god of the Moabites, and its location was the Mount of Olives, and he built another high place dedicated to the god "Molech," god of the children of Ammon. Thus the high place of Chemosh was north of Jerusalem and the high place of Molech south of it. By these high places Solomon fell into many sins:
1- He defied God and provoked Him by setting up pagan worship in opposition to the house of God.
2- He caused his people to stumble and led them astray, because he encouraged them to worship idols in addition to the worship of God.
3- He made the people of God lose their standing as a good example to the surrounding nations, and God became merely one god among many gods.

And we did not hear that when Solomon married Pharaoh's daughter he set up temples for her pagan gods, and perhaps this means that he was able to convince her to worship God, so she joined his people; but his immersion in desires and the multitude of women weakened his will and his spiritual fervor, so he yielded to the pressures of his other wives and introduced their pagan worship into his country.

Solomon was not content with these two high places for pagan gods, but built the like of them for the gods of his pagan wives, who used to burn incense and sacrifice to their gods, and by this Solomon introduced idol worship and sacrificing on the high places, which remained in the life of his descendants for hundreds of years until Josiah the good king, who appeared near the end of the kingdom, that is, shortly before the captivity, and removed these forms of worship completely.
Of course Solomon's deviation into the worship of idols aroused God's anger against him, for the following reasons:
1- Because God appeared to him twice in a vision and warned him against idol worship (ch. 3:5-14, ch. 9:1-9).
2- God gave him wisdom that surpassed everyone before him and after him.
3- He granted him more wealth than all the kings of the earth of his days.

God announced His punishment of Solomon because of his breaking the covenant with God and his rejecting His commandments. And He told him, I will surely rend the kingdom from thee, and will give it to thy servant. He means that God will permit it to be divided into two parts, and the larger part of it will be taken by Jeroboam the son of Nebat, Solomon's servant.
And God announced this punishment either by the hand of a prophet such as Ahijah, or by the mouth of the high priest, or in some way such as his hearing a voice from heaven.

And the honor of the saints appears: for David's sake and for the sake of the name of God called upon His Temple in Jerusalem, the holy city, God promised Solomon to postpone the punishment to the reign of his son and to leave one tribe under his rule. The one tribe mentioned is the tribe of Benjamin, which was a small tribe adjacent to the tribe of Judah, so the two joined and became one kingdom under the name of the kingdom of Judah.

And God intended by this punishment not to take vengeance on Solomon but to call him to repentance. Many of the Fathers see that he actually repented after hearing God's punishment and wrote the Book of Ecclesiastes, in which he shows the vanity of the world and his concern to keep God's commandments.
And leaving the tribe of Benjamin with Judah under the rule of David's offspring had two purposes:
1- The continuation of the worship of God in His Temple in Jerusalem.
2- The continuation of David's offspring until Christ, the Savior of the world, should come from it.

Be sure that God loves you even while you are in your sin, so He sends you many blessings or punishment in the form of various afflictions so that you may repent. So return to Him quickly to regain your sonship and enjoy His care and love.

The peace that surrounded Solomon during the period of his reign until now was from the arrangement of the Lord, who made all around him be at peace with him, as the Scripture says: "When a man's ways please the LORD, he maketh even his enemies to be at peace with him" (Prov 16:7). But when he sinned, divine grace left him, and enemies began to appear to him who opposed him, and perhaps they had been there but were weak before the power of God that supported him; and among these enemies was Hadad the Edomite, who was an Edomite prince.

And we notice that Solomon's wealth and his concern for the multitude of horses and chariots did not protect and support him, because it is God who protects His children if they keep His commandments and stay away from desires.
To bury the slain: what is meant is the slain from the children of Israel.

David's army attacked Edom and defeated them and took their country and placed soldiers subject to him in it, but afterward Edom rebelled against David and killed some of his soldiers, so David's army attacked it under the leadership of Joab, and they buried the slain Jewish soldiers and wiped out every male in Edom, because of its rebellion, and that within six months.

Some men of the Edomite royal guard were able to flee to Egypt, and they took with them the princes, and Hadad, who was a little boy. Egypt was not on good terms with the children of Israel in the days of David as it became later in the days of Solomon, because of his marriage to Pharaoh's daughter.
Midian: a part of the Sinai Peninsula, extending from the Gulf of Aqaba to northern Sinai.
Paran: a desert south of Judah, east of Beersheba and north of Sinai.
