Hadad and the men with him took an unfamiliar route in the journeys from Palestine to Egypt, to escape from David's soldiers who were pursuing them, so they went by way of "Midian" until they reached "Paran," and from there the inhabitants of Paran guided them to the way to Egypt, where they presented themselves to the king of Egypt, asking to take refuge with him, and Pharaoh was very generous with Hadad and gave him a house and assigned him daily food and gave him land.
Tahpenes: the wife of the Pharaoh who belonged to the twenty-first dynasty and was a contemporary of Solomon.

Pharaoh was impressed by Hadad, so he honored him and gave him in marriage the sister of his wife the queen, and Hadad had by her a male child whom he named "Genubath," and the child was weaned and was brought up with Pharaoh's sons in his palace. Pharaoh allied himself with Hadad by marriage so that he would be an ally to him in this region.

Hadad remained in Egypt, a fugitive from the face of David, until he learned of his death and of that of Joab the captain of his army, so he decided to return to his homeland and asked Pharaoh's permission for that, and this was in the early part of Solomon's reign, and he began to stir up the Edomites against Solomon..

Despite Pharaoh's honoring of Hadad, Hadad asked him to let him return to his country after David's death, and Pharaoh tried to keep him, but he insisted, because he wanted to avenge his country. Hadad began with weak attacks on the children of Israel at first, but they increased with time, and that was after Solomon's fall and God's punishment of him.

Hadadezer king of Zobah: David had fought him before and defeated him. He tried again with the help of other kings who allied with him, and David defeated them also and slew their commander "Shobach," and the rest submitted to David (2 Sam 10:6-19). Zobah: a great kingdom among the kingdoms of "Aram" west of the Euphrates.

The second adversary was Rezon the son of Eliadah, one of the commanders of Hadadezer king of Zobah, who fled after David defeated them, and Rezon and all who were with him continued to fear David because of his godliness and God's support of him, and then after him Solomon, when he worshiped God with all his heart. But when Solomon turned aside to the worship of idols, God withdrew His support from him, and Rezon began to oppose Solomon.

When Rezon fled from the face of David, he formed a band to which he gathered many men, and he began to attack some countries and take their spoils until he grew strong and was able to attack Damascus and take possession of it.
Aram: it is present-day Syria.

By Rezon's reigning over Damascus he gained control of the kingdom of Aram, whose capital is Damascus. Damascus was a commercial city on a trade route, and by Rezon's reigning over it Solomon lost much in his trade, and Aram was no longer subject to him but became a center of opposition to him from the north of his country, in addition to the opposition of Hadad the Edomite to him from the south (v. 14). And Rezon bore hatred for Solomon because of what David had done in his country, so he opposed Solomon fiercely.

Keep God's commandments so that He may keep you from your enemies the demons, who want to devour you but fear you if you hold fast to God. So trust in your strength as long as you are with God, and do not be concerned about the threats of the wicked, for God is able to rescue you from them.

entries.section: (4) A prophecy of the splitting of the kingdom

paragraphs.text: Zeredah: a city located west of the Jordan.

A third adversary of Solomon appeared, Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who was one of his servants and was from the tribe of Ephraim and from the city of Zeredah; his mother's name was Zeruah and she was a widow. The tribe of Ephraim was the largest of the tribes in number and was much given to rebellion since the era of the judges, in the days of Gideon and after him Jephthah the Gileadite, and then they rebelled against David. Thus enemies of Solomon appear not only from outside, like Hadad and Rezon, but also from within, that is, from his servants.

entries.section: (4) A prophecy of the splitting of the kingdom

paragraphs.text: Lifted up his hand against the king: rebelled against him.

The story of Jeroboam's rebellion began from the time Solomon built Millo, which is a fortified part of Jerusalem, and repaired the city of David also, which is another part of Jerusalem. Jeroboam's industry in work and strong personality appeared, so that Solomon trusted him and appointed him over the workers from the house of Joseph, that is, the tribes of Ephraim and Manasseh, because he was an Ephraimite like them. And Jeroboam was strong in his leadership of the tribe of Ephraim, because forced labor is a hated thing, in addition to the tribe of Ephraim feeling that it had more right to the kingship than the tribe of Judah from which Solomon came. So how could they be subjected to forced labor for a king who was not of their tribe?

entries.section: (4) A prophecy of the splitting of the kingdom

paragraphs.text: Shiloh: located in the hill country of Ephraim, north of Jerusalem at a distance of 19 km, and it was the seat of the tabernacle of meeting for a long time, from the days of Joshua until David (Josh 18:1). It happened at that time that Jeroboam was going out of the city of Jerusalem, probably to carry out some mission he had been charged with, and the prophet Ahijah the Shilonite met him, and the prophet was wearing a new garment. The prophet took off the garment he was wearing and tore it into twelve pieces, according to the number of the tribes of Israel. And in order that God might declare that He is the one who made the decision to tear the kingdom, He had His prophet, who represents Him, tear his garment into twelve pieces, that is, God, the true King of the kingdom, would permit it to be torn into two parts, the first including ten tribes and the second two tribes. This reminds us of what Saul did when he caught hold of Samuel's garment and it tore, and then Samuel said that God would tear the kingdom from him, that is, Saul would die and one who deserves it, David, would reign over it (1 Sam 15:27, 28).

entries.section: (4) A prophecy of the splitting of the kingdom

paragraphs.text: The prophet said to Jeroboam, Take ten pieces of this garment, and then explained to him what that means, namely that the Lord, the God of Israel, would permit the kingdom of Israel to be divided, after all the tribes had been subject to Solomon, and that Jeroboam would take ten tribes to reign over.

entries.section: (4) A prophecy of the splitting of the kingdom

paragraphs.text: But because of the Lord's love for David and His esteem for Jerusalem, the city chosen for His name to be upon it, He decided to keep one tribe continuing in submission to Solomon, the tribe of Benjamin, in addition to the tribe of Judah from which Solomon came.

entries.section: (4) A prophecy of the splitting of the kingdom

paragraphs.text: The Lord declared the reason for His permitting the tearing of the kingdom, which is Israel's forsaking the living God and their worshiping Ashtoreth the god of Sidon, and Chemosh the god of Moab, and Milcom the god of the children of Ammon, and thus Israel had turned aside, under Solomon's rule, from the way of the Lord, and had not done what is pleasing to the Lord and had not kept the statutes and judgments that He had given it as it had kept them during the reign of David. And because of Solomon's concern for the pagan gods, he caused many of his people to fall into idol worship.

When a trial comes upon you, examine yourself lest the cause be your sin, and repent of it, and know that God is compassionate and ready to forgive you and remove the trial from you and turn it to your good.

entries.section: (4) A prophecy of the splitting of the kingdom

paragraphs.text: Again the Lord declares His faithfulness to His covenants to David and His love for him, in that the separation of the tribes would not take place in Solomon's lifetime, but He would leave him king over all the tribes of the children of Israel all the days of his life. Perhaps God wants by this to give him a chance to repent and not be occupied with the division of the kingdom in his days, for God appreciates Solomon's labors in building the Temple and all his great works. And Solomon most likely repented, as proved by his writing the Book of Ecclesiastes at the end of his life, but God insisted on the division of the kingdom because of the spread of idol worship in which many of the kings who were of Solomon's offspring walked.

entries.section: (4) A prophecy of the splitting of the kingdom

paragraphs.text: The Lord repeats mention of what He will do in the future, that this division would take place in the days of the reign of Solomon's son, and the Lord would give ten tribes to Jeroboam to reign over.

entries.section: (4) A prophecy of the splitting of the kingdom

paragraphs.text: The Lord leaves one tribe so that the remembrance of David may remain before Him all the days in the city of Jerusalem, which He chose to put His name there, and Jerusalem did not fall into captivity until the end, after all the tribes. And as David was a shining star in God's hand, so his offspring will be a lamp throughout the days, and even if some of his offspring walked in evil and the light of the lamp grew dim in those times, yet this lamp shines mightily in the person of Christ, who comes from the offspring of David to reign forever over the hearts of those who believe in Him.

entries.section: (4) A prophecy of the splitting of the kingdom

paragraphs.text: The Lord gives the kingship to Jeroboam and grants him all that he desires, and he will be king over Israel. We see here that God announces the name of the new, split-off kingdom, that is, of the ten tribes, which is the kingdom of Israel, and God knew that Jeroboam desired the kingship and that his whole tribe desired the kingship, so He gave him this kingship, but on condition of submission to His commandments (v. 38).

entries.section: (4) A prophecy of the splitting of the kingdom

paragraphs.text: Here the Lord sets for Jeroboam a condition for the continuance of His blessing to him, which is keeping the commandment and walking in the ways of the Lord and doing what is right in His eyes, with observing the statutes and ordinances of the Law, as David did before, and then the hand of the Lord would be with him, so He would bring stability to the kingdom and establish him in the rule of Israel, he and his offspring after him. Although God knows by His foreknowledge that Jeroboam is wicked and will worship idols, yet He commands him, in the hope that he may believe and live with God.

entries.section: (4) A prophecy of the splitting of the kingdom

paragraphs.text: And if God will humble the offspring of David for their sins, not only by their having a small kingdom, the two tribes of Judah and Benjamin only, but also by His permitting them to be disciplined in captivity, yet the captivity will not continue all the days, but they will return from it and unite again with the rest of the tribes; and then He gives them hope also that this humiliation will end with the birth of Christ and His salvation of mankind, that is, the true offspring of David, who are all the believers.

entries.section: (4) A prophecy of the splitting of the kingdom

paragraphs.text: Solomon learned of Ahijah's prophecy to Jeroboam, so he asked for Jeroboam to be arrested in order to kill him, and Jeroboam fled to Shishak king of Egypt. The strange thing is that Solomon did not repent before this prophecy, and all he tried was to kill Jeroboam, and of course he could not, because the prophecy is from God.

And it is understood from (v. 26) that Jeroboam, after hearing Ahijah's prophecy, became proud, and perhaps he gathered around him some troublemakers and rebels against Solomon and began to declare his rebellion against the king. This is what made Solomon seek to kill him, which shows the extent of Jeroboam's pride, impulsiveness and wickedness; for God permitted Jeroboam's reigning as a discipline for His people who worshiped idols, perhaps that they might repent.

The writer of the book refers here to other details concerning what Solomon did during the period of his reign and his wisdom for which he was famous, and these details are recorded in a book called "the acts of Solomon," a historical book, perhaps the chronicles that the kings write for themselves, or that someone wrote about the history of Solomon, and it is different from the books recorded in the Bible.

The period of Solomon's reign in Jerusalem over all Israel was 40 years, after which Solomon died and was buried in the city of David his father, and his son Rehoboam reigned in his stead. Solomon's age at his death did not exceed sixty, because the Fathers say that he was anointed king while young, and in all likelihood he had not passed twenty. And although his father David endured many troubles from Saul and suffered from various wars with the surrounding nations in addition to troubles from his children, God blessed him and gave him peace of heart and he reigned 40 years, but he lived longer than Solomon, for God gave him a life of seventy years.
Thus we find that Solomon fell into many errors and received punishment from the very same sins and arising from them, as appears in the following:
1- He multiplied the acquiring of horses, contrary to the Law, so the horses and chariots of the enemies attacked the kingdom in the reign of his son Rehoboam.
2- He acquired much gold that the enemies desired, so they attacked the kingdom after his death in various ages and took it.

3- He multiplied marriages, and they turned his heart to the worship of idols, so he set up forms of worship for them in Jerusalem and around it and by this led his people astray, and the Lord was angry with him.

4- He used forced labor, hated by the people, to carry out his huge projects, so his people were troubled and killed Adoram, who was in charge of the forced labor, and rose up against Rehoboam his son, and the kingdom was divided by the hand of Jeroboam, who had been in charge of the forced labor.

Do not be drawn to the desire of sin and its pleasures, lest you be struck by its punishment that results from it, in addition to God's anger against you, so that you lose your peace and forfeit your eternity. And if you fall, return to God by repentance so that you do not remain in your error after the devil.
The division of the kingdom

entries.section: (1) Rehoboam reigns and consults the elders and the young men

paragraphs.text: Shechem: a city in the tribe of Ephraim, 50 km north of Jerusalem, now called Nablus; it is one of the cities of refuge in which the Levites lived (Josh 20:7), and it is considered a middle place among the tribes of the children of Israel. Joshua had set up an altar, and near it are the mountains Gerizim and Ebal, on which the blessings and the curses were proclaimed (Josh 8:33-35). Rehoboam: he became king at the age of 41, the son of an Ammonite wife of Solomon (ch. 14:21), and perhaps the firstborn son of Solomon, and he was not wise despite his advanced age, and we understand from this that Solomon did not care for the upbringing of his children and did not charge them to keep God's commandments as David did.

The representatives of the tribes went to Shechem to enthrone Rehoboam the son of Solomon as king. And here we notice the pressure of the tribes on Rehoboam to reign in Shechem, which is in Ephraim, in order to take him away from Jerusalem, which is in Judah, where his father and grandfather reigned and where the army that supports him is. The tribes planned to demand their own demands of Rehoboam, so that if he refused it would be easy to depose him, far from his tribe and his army that is in Judah. And because Rehoboam was weak in character, he yielded to their opinion, and they made him king in Shechem.

entries.section: (1) Rehoboam reigns and consults the elders and the young men

paragraphs.text: The yoke: the crosspiece of wood that is placed on the necks of the two animals that pull farming implements, and "your father made our yoke grievous" means that he pressed us and wearied us greatly.
Jeroboam had a strong and rebellious personality, so Solomon tried to kill him, and therefore he fled to Egypt (ch. 11:

40.) When he heard, while in Egypt, of Solomon's death, he felt reassured and tried to return, and what encouraged him to do so was that those among his people who loved him sent for him to return and support them in demanding of the new king Rehoboam a lightening of the taxes and the harsh orders upon them, so he actually returned and led them in demanding of Rehoboam that he lighten his bondage over them, and they made this a condition for their submission to and service of the new king. And the people in this demand forgot the merits of Solomon's rule and his wisdom and his good organization of the kingdom, so that he gave them peace and they lived securely without wars. And we notice also that they did not care about rejecting the worship of idols that had spread in the kingdom because of Solomon's laxity, for their aim was their material comfort and not attachment to God and the rejection of strange gods.

And we find that Solomon had earlier cared to fortify himself, so he married Pharaoh's daughter to ensure Egypt's support for him and did not place all his reliance on God, and now there comes the rebel Jeroboam, whom Egypt had sheltered, to divide the kingdom in the reign of his son Rehoboam. For God alone is able to protect man and establish kings in their kingdom.

Place your reliance on God above everything, then use all the means as instruments in God's hand to solve your problems, and if some of them fail or are delayed, do not be troubled, because God alone is able to support you and keep you from every evil.

entries.section: (1) Rehoboam reigns and consults the elders and the young men

paragraphs.text: Rehoboam asked the representatives of the tribes for time to think, so that he could consult with his counselors about the matter, and they would return to him after three days, that he might tell them his decision in the matter.

entries.section: (1) Rehoboam reigns and consults the elders and the young men

paragraphs.text: Rehoboam began by consulting the wise elders with experience, who had assisted his father Solomon throughout his life, asking them what answer he should give the people.

And we notice that Rehoboam did not resort to prayer first, as his grandfather David used to do, for God is the true King of the kingdom, but what he did is considered a kind of wisdom, since he was not hasty in answering the people and took care to consult wise counselors.
It is good that you consult others who have opinion and counsel regarding the works you undertake, but it befits you first and before everything to seek God's counsel.

entries.section: (1) Rehoboam reigns and consults the elders and the young men

paragraphs.text: The elders answered him that if he would pledge himself to the people to look after their interests and win them to him with gentle words, they would be subject to him all his life. By his showing submission to their demands and pledging concern for their comfort, he would make them attached to him and serve him faithfully. And these are the qualities of a wise king, and this is what the Lord Christ, the King of kings, did, for He served His people not only by teaching them and healing their diseases but by laying down His life for them, so the hearts of His children became attached to Him and they gave their lives even to martyrdom.

entries.section: (1) Rehoboam reigns and consults the elders and the young men

paragraphs.text: Rehoboam wanted also to listen to what his young friends said, among whom he had grown up and from whom he chose new counselors, and perhaps they shared with him his life of luxury and some amusement, or recklessness. It is understood from his consulting the young men that he was not at ease with the counsel of the elders, perhaps because of his unwillingness to reduce his financial resources from taxes and his lack of concern for the interests and problems of the people.

entries.section: (1) Rehoboam reigns and consults the elders and the young men

paragraphs.text: The little finger: the smallest finger of the hand.
The loins: the lower part of the back, that is, what a person sits on.

The counsel of the young men was entirely different from the counsel of the elders, for they advised the king to speak to the people with arrogance and harshness, to frighten them and ensure their submission, and to say to them that my little finger is thicker than my father's loins, and this was a well-known, common proverb at that time, meaning I am stronger and harsher than he. And if my father enslaved you and subjected you to forced labor in his works harshly by beating you with whips, then whoever neglects his work or tries to rebel, I will chastise him with scorpions, which not only hurt like whips but poison the human body and kill it, and some see that scorpions are a kind of whip with pieces of iron that tear the skin severely.
And here we see the causes that led to Rehoboam's deviation, which are:
1- He was pampered, so he had no long-suffering, and could not contain his people and their demands.
2- His mother was an Ammonite, so she did not teach him God's commandments and to take refuge in Him.
3- It is not mentioned that his father cared for his upbringing, because of his preoccupation with his desires.
4- He was proud, so he had no readiness to learn and to be a disciple at the hands of the elders and their counsel.
5- He was not wise enough to distinguish good counsel from bad.
It is fitting for us to choose our counselors from tried elders of pure spiritual conduct, and to listen to them and act on their counsel, and not hand over our will to inexperienced bad friends.
The representatives of the people came, and Jeroboam with them, to Rehoboam, as the king had set for them on the third day, to listen to what he had decided regarding their request.

Rehoboam used harsh words in addressing the people, following the counsel of the young men and forsaking the counsel of the elders, and said: my father was harsh to you and I will add to this harshness; my father used whips to subdue you, but I will use scorpions for that.

Rehoboam rejected the demands of the people with arrogance and folly, so God's grace left him, and thus the word of God by the mouth of His Shilonite prophet about the tearing of the kingdom was fulfilled (ch. 11:29-39).

What portion have we in David?: the meaning is that we have no rights with the house of David, which is represented by the unjust Rehoboam and his father, the harsh Solomon, and therefore this is considered a declaration of secession.

To your tents, O Israel: a clear call for the ten tribes to split from the tribe of Judah by returning to their dwellings to look for a king for themselves, and none remained with Judah except the tribe of Benjamin (v. 21) and some individuals of the children of Israel adjoining them, such as the Simeonites.

Now see to thine own house, David: they address David as the most important figure who appeared on the throne of the children of Israel, and (see) how his kingdom was torn apart in the reign of his grandson Rehoboam.

When it became clear to the people that the king rejected their demands, they declared their rebellion against him and against the house of David and decided to withdraw from the assembly and to split from the tribe of Judah. Or Rehoboam the king, who is of the offspring of David the son of Jesse, and what is meant by tents is the dwellings of the ten tribes.
There remained to Rehoboam only the people living in the cities of the tribe of Judah and their neighbors from the nearby tribes, namely the tribe of Benjamin and some of the tribe of Simeon.

King Rehoboam remained in Shechem, the place where they had made him king, and paid no attention to the words of rebellion that the delegates of the tribes led by Jeroboam had spoken, but continued to carry on his administration of the kingdom as if nothing had happened in the meeting with the tribes, and sent Adoram, who was in charge of subjecting the people to forced labor in the works the kingdom needed, so the people rose up against him in all fury and stoned him until he died. Of course this was an unwise act on Rehoboam's part, to send Adoram at this time, but his pride and impulsiveness made him act this way, especially since forced labor is a thing unwanted by the people and heavy on them, and it would have been better for him to send delegates from himself to come to an understanding and try to reunite the kingdom. At last Rehoboam became aware of the seriousness of the situation and of the tribes' having actually split from him, so he mounted his chariot and fled from Shechem to Jerusalem, to take refuge there among his tribe of Judah, because he feared that the people would stone him as they had Adoram.

May you humble yourself before God when any trial meets you and seek Him with lowliness and faith, and He will guide you to the truth whatever your errors may be. For repentance with humility pours upon you God's mercies and forgiveness, and He rescues you and guides you and keeps you.
Israel: what is meant is the ten tribes.

This was the beginning of the separation of the ten tribes of Israel from the kingdom of Judah until the day of the writing of this book. From here we see that the division of the kingdom into two kingdoms took place for the following reasons:
1- The failure to turn back from the worship of idols, which Solomon began, by repentance and cleaving to God, so the throne of David lost God's protection and blessing.
2- Rehoboam's not submitting to the counsel of the experienced elders.
3- Rehoboam's lack of feeling for the people's feelings, and even his threatening them, which provoked them greatly and called them to division.
4- A discipline for the tribes of Judah and Benjamin for their preoccupation with the worship of idols that Solomon introduced instead of the worship of God in His Temple.

5- A discipline for the ten tribes for their preoccupation with the worship of idols, so they were deprived of going up to Jerusalem, and Jeroboam seduced them to the worship of the golden calves and the forsaking of God.

Jeroboam was well known to the children of Israel from his past efforts in the service of King Solomon and carrying out his building works, and they also knew of Solomon's hatred of him when he learned of the prophecy of his taking rule over ten of the tribes of Israel, so they decided to make him king over them. And of the tribes none remained in submission to Rehoboam except the tribe of Judah and Benjamin with it, v. 21.) And here we record three warnings from God of the division of the kingdom:
1- From God to Solomon (ch. 11:11-13).
2- From Ahijah the prophet to Jeroboam (ch. 11:29-32).
3- From Shemaiah to Rehoboam (vv. 22-24). And the people's choosing Jeroboam as king over the ten tribes goes back to the following:
1- His distinction in leading the work in the days of Solomon.
2- That he is from the tribe of Ephraim, which is the largest of the tribes in number and has its strength and standing among the tribes.
3- Jeroboam was known to Shishak king of Egypt, and this gives a kind of reassurance of the support of strong Egypt for the new kingdom.

4- The prophecy of Ahijah the Shilonite to Jeroboam of his reigning over the ten tribes, for this gives a sense of God's good pleasure and His blessing of Jeroboam, although it was only a prophecy and God is pleased only with good works. And God permitted this evil as a discipline for Judah and the tribes for their going away from God.
By this the splitting of the kingdom into two kingdoms was accomplished, which are:

1- The kingdom of Judah, which is followed by the tribes of Judah and Benjamin, and whose capital is Jerusalem, and it is called the southern kingdom, and in it is the Temple of God, and its kings reigned by inheritance, that is, all of them from the offspring of David, and their number is 19 kings, some of them righteous and the others wicked, and one wicked queen reigned with them, Athaliah the daughter of Ahab king of Israel, who was not of the offspring of David and was killed after a short time of her reign, that is, the total of those who reigned over Judah is twenty kings and queen. The kingdom of Judah began after the division in the year 931 BC and ended with the Babylonian captivity and the destruction of Jerusalem in the year 586 BC, so the age of the kingdom was 345 years.

2- The kingdom of Israel, which includes the remaining ten tribes and is called the northern kingdom, and its capital was first Shechem, then Penuel, then Tirzah, and finally Samaria, which remained its capital until its end. Its kings were all wicked and in most cases were not by inheritance, and 19 kings reigned over it. It began in the year 931 BC and ended with the Assyrian captivity in the year 722 BC, so the age of the kingdom was 209 years.

The kings of Judah and the kings of Israel were in enmity and fought from the beginning of the two kingdoms until the time of Asa king of Judah and Omri king of Israel. Then in the second period they were allied and cooperating, and this is from the reign of Jehoshaphat king of Judah and Ahab king of Israel until Ahaziah the son of Jehoshaphat and Ahaziah and Joram kings of Israel; that is, the period of peace between them was short, and then came after it the third stage, in which the two kingdoms were estranged and wars were between them until the end of the kingdom of Israel.
It is noticed that the kingdom of Israel ended before the kingdom of Judah by about 136 years.
Note: the years in the Old Testament are all approximate.

entries.section: (3) The Lord prevents Rehoboam from fighting the tribes

paragraphs.text: In an attempt to regain what he had foolishly lost, and thinking that he was able to confront the rebellion of the tribes, Rehoboam gathered an army of 180 thousand men from the tribes of Judah and Benjamin against Israel, to fight Israel (the ten tribes).

entries.section: (3) The Lord prevents Rehoboam from fighting the tribes

paragraphs.text: Shemaiah: a prophet contemporary with Rehoboam and a chronicler of his reign.

The Lord commanded Shemaiah the prophet to declare to Rehoboam and all the people of Judah and Benjamin that the splitting of the ten tribes was by God's permission, so they should not try to fight them, because this was a divine discipline so that they might all repent, and they obeyed God and each returned to his house. And here we see a virtue appearing in Rehoboam, which is obedience to God in the end. If only he had prayed and known what God's will was and obeyed Him from the beginning, but unfortunately he did not continue in obeying God and fought the tribes.

Be obedient to God's commandments that you read in the Holy Bible and hear in the Church, and so you will rescue yourself from the snares of the demons and walk uprightly and keep your peace in your heart always.
Mount Ephraim: what is meant is the lands of the tribe of Ephraim, which are full of mountains.

Penuel: a city east of the Jordan at a distance of four miles, in which God appeared to Jacob (Gen 32:30). Gideon had pulled down its tower and killed its inhabitants (Judg 8:8, 9, 17), and then Jeroboam, the first of the kings of Israel, rebuilt and fortified it.

After Jeroboam split off with the ten tribes, he became king over them and took Shechem, in which Rehoboam had been, as the capital of his kingdom, to declare to the tribes that he was the new king and not Rehoboam. And he took care to build up the city, that is, to fortify it and complete its buildings, so that it might be the capital of his kingdom. And afterward he took as the capital of his kingdom Penuel. Thus Jeroboam tried to make the seat of his kingdom in cities that had spiritual memories for the people, to gain their love and their loyalty to him. And this was a political act on his part and not love of God or of the holy places.

Jeroboam was a man far from God, for despite his hearing a clear prophecy from Ahijah the Shilonite that God would give him the ten tribes, and that was actually accomplished, anxiety was still within him, so he thought with a human mind, not relying on God, and said that if the people went to offer their sacrifices in the Temple at Jerusalem, as the Law prescribes on the various occasions and especially at the three feasts, namely the feast of Passover and the harvest and Tabernacles (Deut 16), longing would take hold of them for the days of the unity of the tribes, and they would decide to submit to Rehoboam king of Judah and get rid of him and kill him.

A person sometimes forgets that all the good things he enjoys are a divine gift, so he fears their loss and seeks to retain them by human tricks, whose vanity he soon discovers, and he knows then that the Lord is the Giver and that He alone is able to preserve His gift.

Jeroboam did not take refuge in God in solving this problem, which was his fear of the people's leaving him, and forgot God's promise to give him the ten tribes, which He had actually given him, so he thought in a human way and consulted his counselors, and made two calves of gold, to show the greatness of his gods, and to resemble the house of God covered with gold, and this sin the counselors shared with Rehoboam. And he said to the people, these are your gods which brought you up out of the land of Egypt, that is, these two calves are an image of Jehovah, and he put one of them in the north at Dan and the other in the south at Bethel so that it would be easy for all the inhabitants of the kingdom of Israel to reach them. And by Jeroboam's saying these are your gods that brought you out of the land of Egypt, and not saying your God, he led the people to fall into the worship of many idols. And the counselors' suggestion to Jeroboam that he set up two golden calves shows the extent of the spread of idol worship among the people and his counselors because of Solomon.

And the counselors deceived the people and told them that these calves are an image of Jehovah, and the people believed, and with time they became accustomed to the worship of idols, although the commandment (Ex 20:4) clearly forbade making images because they would lead the people astray from God. And by setting up the two calves Jeroboam committed many errors, which are:
1- He did not trust in God, who had promised him kingship by the hand of Ahijah the Shilonite.
2- He kept the people away from the worship of God in His Temple.
3- He introduced idol worship into the kingdom of Israel in the form of these two calves.
4- This work of his helped in the entry of the gods of the pagan nations into the kingdom of Israel, since it gave them the idea of a plurality of gods.

5- He did not learn from the error of the people in the days of Aaron when he made the golden calf and said to the people, "These be thy gods, O Israel" (Ex 32:4), so God was angry and killed thousands of the people by the hand of Moses.

This was a return to pagan worship, and the people used to go to Dan or Bethel, whichever was nearer to the place of their dwelling, so the matter was a great sin into which Jeroboam fell and into which he made his subject people fall.

Jeroboam continued in his evils, for he was not content with setting up the two calves but also set up altars on the high places, that is, the hills and plateaus, for the worship of God, contrary to the commandments of God, who commanded that worship be in His holy Temple only in Jerusalem. And when the Levites saw his immersion in evil, they left the cities of the kingdom of Israel and went to Jerusalem, so as not to anger God by taking part in these evil forms of worship (2 Chr 11:13, 14). Then Jeroboam continued in his evil, and set up priests and ministers for these strange forms of worship from the other tribes besides the tribe of Levi. And his saying "of the lowest of the people" means from the various classes, even the lowly among them, in an attempt to draw the hearts of the people toward him, by having priests be from all classes, and in all this he neglected God and rejected His commandments.
Persisting in his evil, Jeroboam made a feast for his gods that he had made in Bethel and Dan.

And he set this feast on the fifteenth day of the eighth month, as a substitute for the feast of Tabernacles, which God commanded after the feast of the harvest and which is on the fifteenth day of the seventh month. He put it a month after the feast of Tabernacles because the harvest is later in the northern kingdom than in the southern, but the real motive behind holding this feast at this time was to keep the people away from the feasts that God commanded. And here Jeroboam sinned by instituting a feast from his own ideas and not from God, for the worship of his idols. He concentrated the worship in Bethel, because Jeroboam himself used to pray in this place, as the Book of Amos tells us (Amos 7:13), and Jeroboam offered sacrifices in Bethel, perhaps offering them himself, and this is a usurpation of the priesthood, and all this had the outward form of the worship of God but was in truth the worship of idols, and by this Jeroboam led his people astray after the worship of idols and made all the kings who came after him fall into the same errors.

And we notice that God did not strike him with leprosy like King Uzziah (2 Kgs 15:5), because Jeroboam did not go up to burn incense on God's holy altar, as Uzziah did, but went up to an altar of idols, which needs no priesthood. And we notice that he makes light of God and deceives by pretending to be a good king who does not want to burden his people with travelling to Jerusalem, whereas the truth is that he wants to keep his people away from Rehoboam lest they submit to him.
And perhaps among the things that encouraged Jeroboam to worship idols was what Solomon, the king before him, did in spreading pagan forms of worship among the children of Israel.

If you fall into an error, examine yourself and repent, so that you do not persist in it and the error drags you into many other errors. Humble yourself and seek God, and He will rescue you and bring you back to Him.
Prophecy of the destruction of the pagan altars (1) Prophecy about Josiah (vv. 1-10)

1- And, behold, there came a man of God out of Judah by the word of the LORD unto Bethel: and Jeroboam stood by the altar to burn incense. 2- And he cried against the altar in the word of the LORD, and said, O altar, altar, thus saith the LORD; Behold, a child shall be born unto the house of David, Josiah by name; and upon thee shall he offer the priests of the high places that burn incense upon thee, and men's bones shall be burnt upon thee. 3- And he gave a sign the same day, saying, This is the sign which the LORD hath spoken; Behold, the altar shall be rent, and the ashes that are upon it shall be poured out. 4- And it came to pass, when king Jeroboam heard the saying of the man of God, which had cried against the altar in Bethel, that he put forth his hand from the altar, saying, Lay hold on him. And his hand, which he put forth against him, dried up, so that he could not pull it in again to him. 5- The altar also was rent, and the ashes poured out from the altar, according to the sign which the man of God had given by the word of the LORD. 6- And the king answered and said unto the man of God, Intreat now the face of the LORD thy God, and pray for me, that my hand may be restored me again. And the man of God besought the LORD, and the king's hand was restored him again, and became as it was before. 7- And the king said unto the man of God, Come home with me, and refresh thyself, and I will give thee a reward. 8- And the man of God said unto the king, If thou wilt give me half thine house, I will not go in with thee, neither will I eat bread nor drink water in this place: 9- For so was it charged me by the word of the LORD, saying, Eat no bread, nor drink water, nor turn again by the same way that thou camest. 10- So he went another way, and returned not by the way that he came to Bethel.

Jeroboam made himself a priest and stood at the altar burning incense, so the Lord sent him a prophet from Judah to warn him, that he might have no excuse for persisting in his sins. God wanted to alert Jeroboam, so He sent him from Judah, that is, from His holy house, one to rebuke him for his evil. For God does not leave Himself without a witness. The name of the man of God is not mentioned, because he disobeyed God's commandment, as appears from (vv. 19, 20).
Josiah: the son of Amon king of Judah, who took the throne at the age of 8 years and walked according to the Law, and so opposed pagan worship.

The prophet stood at the altar where Jeroboam was burning incense and cried out with all boldness, calling in a loud voice against the altar built of stones, perhaps so that the heart of Jeroboam and of those around him of the people of Israel, whose hearts had become stony, might be moved and pay heed to God's words and stop persisting in their evils by worshiping idols. He did not speak to Jeroboam or to those standing around him, because they had persisted in evil, but spoke to the altar, that is, the stones, because they are better than these wicked men. And the man of God prophesied about Josiah king of Judah, about 350 years before his birth, that he would rise up and tear down the pagan altars and burn the bones of those who burn incense before them (2 Kgs 23:15-20), that is, defile these altars, because the bones of the dead in the Law of Moses defile whoever touches them, to declare that these altars are unclean in God's sight and were not able to protect the priests and those who worshiped before them from death. So he declares God's anger against these pagan altars and therefore demands that the people remove them and return to the worship of God in His Temple in Jerusalem, and if they do not remove them, there will come one who will remove them, namely King Josiah, but everyone who worshiped before these altars will be judged.

And so that the people might believe what this prophet was saying, since God's word would be fulfilled 350 years later by the hand of Josiah, he told them that God would give them a sign now so that they would believe his words, perhaps they would repent and turn back from the worship of idols, and this sign was that the altar before which Jeroboam stood would be rent and the ashes on it poured out, indicating thereby that God's word is able to shake stony hearts and scatter the defilement that has clung to them.

When King Jeroboam heard the prophet's words, he was not moved or aware of his error, but on the contrary he was enraged and left off offering the sacrifice that was on the altar, and stretched out his hand and pointed to the prophet, that they might seize him so that he might chastise him or kill him, but God defended His prophet with power, for He made Jeroboam's hand dry up, so he cried out, and all who stood there felt the power of God that was with the prophet and that cannot be resisted.

God fulfilled His word by splitting the altar into two parts and the ashes fell from it, and this sign showed God's power, so that all who stood there were afraid, but unfortunately this did not move them to repentance.

Jeroboam was afraid and alarmed when his hand dried up, and asked the man of God to intercede in prayer for him that his hand might be healed, and indeed the prophet did not become angry or desire vengeance on Jeroboam but besought the Lord, and the king's hand was restored whole as it was. Thus God called Jeroboam and those around him to repentance by four things:
1- The prophet's prophecy about Josiah, who would remove the altars and kill their priests.
2- The splitting of the altar and the falling of the ashes from it.
3- God's making Jeroboam's hand dry up.
4- The healing of Jeroboam's hand that had dried up and its return to health.

But unfortunately Jeroboam said to the prophet "Intreat the face of the LORD thy God" and did not try to repent and return to God that He might be his own God, and even after his healing he did not repent, and in this he resembles the pagan Pharaoh, who used to say to Moses, Pray to your God that He take away the plagues from us.
The king asked the man of God to come to his palace to eat and that he might reward him for the healing of his hand.

Thus by the power of God Jeroboam feared and respected the man of God and tried to honor him, and this is an attempt to influence the man of God not by threat, as he had pointed to him before to arrest him (v. 4), but by enticement, perhaps that he might change his words, and by this Jeroboam pretended to be attached to God in honoring His prophet, so that the people would not leave him and go to worship God in Jerusalem.

The man of God firmly refused the king's invitation, whatever gift he would give him, for he would not eat bread or drink water in this place, because it is a place full of evil and it is not right to be in it, or to mingle with the wicked, or to eat of what was sacrificed to idols, although this prophet was probably in need of food and drink and may not have had anything with which to buy, but his obedience to God is above everything, so here he clearly refuses everything connected with evil.
And the man of God's accepting the king's hospitality and gifts would mean his tacit approval of the king's evils, and this would be against the prophecy he had declared.

And by this the prophet obeyed God and did not return by the way he came, so that he would not be delayed by the people who saw or heard his prophecy and miracles, for he does the work of God clearly and with power and is not occupied with the people's praise and honoring of him.

Care to carry out God's commandments, and you will enjoy your sense that God is with you, and this will lift you up and occupy you away from the concerns of the world and separate you from its evils and thoughts.
(2) The error of the man of God and his being killed (vv. 11-26)

11- Now there dwelt an old prophet in Bethel; and his sons came and told him all the works that the man of God had done that day in Bethel: the words which he had spoken unto the king, them they told also to their father. 12- And their father said unto them, What way went he? For his sons had seen what way the man of God went, which came from Judah.

13- And he said unto his sons, Saddle me the ass. So they saddled him the ass: and he rode thereon, The man of God's disobedience to the Lord's command 14- And went after the man of God, and found him sitting under an oak: and he said unto him, Art thou the man of God that camest from Judah? And he said, I am. 15- Then he said unto him, Come home with me, and eat bread. 16- And he said, I may not return with thee, nor go in with thee: neither will I eat bread nor drink water with thee in this place: 17- For it was said to me by the word of the LORD, Thou shalt eat no bread nor drink water there, nor turn again to go by the way that thou camest. 18- He said unto him, I am a prophet also as thou art; and an angel spake unto me by the word of the LORD, saying, Bring him back with thee into thine house, that he may eat bread and drink water. But he lied unto him. 19- So he went back with him, and did eat bread in his house, and drank water. 20- And it came to pass, as they sat at the table, that the word of the LORD came unto the prophet that brought him back: 21- And he cried unto the man of God that came from Judah, saying, Thus saith the LORD, Forasmuch as thou hast disobeyed the mouth of the LORD, and hast not kept the commandment which the LORD thy God commanded thee,

22- But camest back, and hast eaten bread and drunk water in the place, of the which the LORD did say to thee, Eat no bread, and drink no water; thy carcase shall not come unto the sepulchre of thy fathers. 23- And it came to pass, after he had eaten bread, and after he had drunk, that he saddled for him the ass, to wit, for the prophet whom he had brought back. 24- And when he was gone, a lion met him by the way, and slew him: and his carcase was cast in the way, and the ass stood by it, the lion also stood by the carcase. 25- And, behold, men passed by, and saw the carcase cast in the way, and the lion standing by the carcase: and they came and told it in the city where the old prophet dwelt.

26- And when the prophet that brought him back from the way heard thereof, he said, It is the man of God, who was disobedient unto the word of the LORD: therefore the LORD hath delivered him unto the lion, which hath torn him, and slain him, according to the word of the LORD, which he spake unto him.

There was an old prophet dwelling in Bethel, who had not himself been present at the preceding events at the pagan altar, but his sons were there, and when they returned they told him what had happened and of the man of God's refusal of the king's invitation and what he had said about the reason for his refusal, so he asked them about the way by which the man of God had departed, and they told him because they had followed him and knew the way. And this old man is a prophet of God, but because of his weakness he did not declare the voice of God in the midst of the evil led by King Jeroboam.

The old man asked his sons to prepare a donkey for him to ride, and went on the road by which the man of God had gone, and found him after some distance sitting under an oak tree, and asked him, Are you the prophet who prophesied at the altar? and he answered, Yes, so he welcomed him and invited him to return to Bethel to eat a meal in his house.

The man of God refused the old man's invitation because God had commanded him not to eat or drink in Bethel, but that he should depart by another way than the one he came by. By this the obedience of the man of God appears, but unfortunately it was a weak obedience that could be given up under pressure, as we will see in the following verses.
Oak: a huge tree with a large shade.

The old man lied to him and claimed that an angel had spoken to him, for he is also a prophet like him, and the angel asked him to take the man of God with him to his house to eat and drink. And this shows the weakness of the old prophet and his neglect of God's commandments. Perhaps out of curiosity he wanted to host the man of God, to learn from him the details of his prophecy, although he could have been content with asking him about it when he saw him under the tree. For though he is a prophet, he is deceitful and a liar and thinks of his personal aims at the expense of God. And by this he causes others to stumble, and the sin of causing stumbling is very grave in God's sight, because by it he destroys others, and therefore God's punishment for it is severe, which is certain destruction if the person does not repent of it.

The man of God was deceived by the venerable appearance of the old man, so he believed his lie and did not consult God in prayer before carrying out what contradicts God's commands, so he disobeyed God and returned with the old man to Bethel and entered his house to eat and rest.

The man of God was inclined to believe because he was hungry and in need of food and drink; thus Satan comes to us with his enticements from the point of weakness that he finds in us, but the Lord Christ gave us the example and model in the temptation on the mountain, when He refused to turn the stones into bread, exposing the tricks of Satan and his enticements. Be careful of your point of weakness and seek God before any action.

While they were eating together in the old man's house, the Lord spoke by the mouth of the old prophet. By this we see God speaking by the mouth of the old man despite his lying, for prophecy is a gift and does not indicate the godliness and righteousness of its possessor, as Balaam prophesied and blessed the people of God (Num 24) and also prophesied about Christ but loved money, so he became a stumbling block to the people of God and perished. And as Caiaphas the high priest in the days of Christ prophesied of the necessity of Christ's death for the redemption of the Jewish nation (Jn 11:51).

The old man told the man of God a true prophecy that God gave him, which was the punishment of the man of God for disobeying God's command when he returned to Bethel, that he would die and would not be buried in his city in the tomb of his fathers. Being buried with the fathers was a matter people cared about at that time, as Jacob asked to be buried with his fathers, and likewise Joseph his son (Gen 50:5, Heb 11:22).
After they finished eating and drinking, the old man prepared the donkey for the prophet of God from Judah to return on it to his homeland.

The man of God set out on the road returning, and behold a lion blocked his way and killed him, and his body remained lying on the road with the lion and the donkey standing beside it, to declare God's anger against whoever disobeys His commands. For when the man of God was fasting and bold in declaring his prophecy before the king, God kept him from the cruelty and violence of Jeroboam and even made the king fear him and try to honor him; but when he ate and cared for his own comfort and neglected God's commandments and disobeyed them, God's punishment came upon him, which was death.

At that time it happened that some people were walking on the same road and saw the body cast on the ground and the lion standing beside it without tampering with it or devouring it, so they came to the city in which the old prophet lived and told what they had seen on the road.

The news reached the ears of the old prophet, and he realized that the body must be the body of the man of God who came from Judah, who disobeyed the Lord's commandment, so He permitted the lion to kill him, in carrying out the divine punishment that he had pronounced by the tongue of the old man, since he disobeyed God's commandment.

The meaning of God's punishment of the prophet is not that He forgot his boldness and obedience in declaring the prophecy before Jeroboam; rather this punishment was to declare the necessity of the fear of God and obedience to Him before the wicked, like Jeroboam and the old man who was slack in declaring the voice of God, for if He does this to His prophets, how much more to those far from Him. This punishment is for the prophet of God because he knows God and it is not right that he disobey Him, for whoever knows more is required to do more, but his salvation in eternity is another matter, and God alone decides it.
(3) The burial of the man of God (vv. 27-34)

27- And he spake to his sons, saying, Saddle me the ass. And they saddled him. 28- And he went and found his carcase cast in the way, and the ass and the lion standing by the carcase: the lion had not eaten the carcase, nor torn the ass. 29- And the prophet took up the carcase of the man of God, and laid it upon the ass, and brought it back: and the old prophet came to the city, to mourn and to bury him.

30- And he laid his carcase in his own grave; and they mourned over him, saying, Alas, my brother! 31- And it came to pass, after he had buried him, that he spake to his sons, saying, When I am dead, then bury me in the sepulchre wherein the man of God is buried; lay my bones beside his bones. 32- For the saying which he cried by the word of the LORD against the altar in Bethel, and against all the houses of the high places which are in the cities of Samaria, shall surely come to pass. 33- After this thing Jeroboam returned not from his evil way, but made again of the lowest of the people priests of the high places: whosoever would, he consecrated him, and he became one of the priests of the high places. 34- And this thing became sin unto the house of Jeroboam, even to cut it off, and to destroy it from off the face of the earth.

The old man asked his sons to prepare the donkey and rode it and went on the road by which the man of God had gone, and found his body cast down and the lion and the donkey standing beside it. The lion's not devouring the body shows that it was sent from God to carry out the punishment and was not an ordinary hungry lion wanting to eat any prey. And the donkey's not fearing the lion and its standing confirms the submission of the animals to carry out God's commands, whereas the man of God did not obey His word and died.

The old man placed the body of the man of God on the donkey and went with it in sorrow to Bethel and declared his grief in the words of lament known at funerals, and then buried him, pained at his death.

Do not grieve after it is too late; this old man made the man of God stumble and deceived him and made him fall into disobeying God, and he died. Therefore do not be hasty in your words and actions, lest you cause others to stumble and destroy them, because your sorrows will not benefit them; so do not be hasty and rush into your opinions or decisions, but seek God before everything.

The old man charged his sons to bury him after his death in the tomb in which the man of God was buried, because when he saw the lion's killing him and not eating his body or tearing the donkey, he was sure of this prophet's prophecy about the destruction of the pagan altars, not only in Bethel but in all the cities of Samaria. Samaria had not yet been built at that time, because it was built by Omri many years later (ch. 16:24), and he made it the capital of the kingdom of Israel, and what is meant by the cities of Samaria is the whole kingdom of Israel, that is, the northern kingdom, and the old man's speaking of the tearing down of the altars in the cities of Samaria, which had not yet been built, confirms that he is a prophet of God and that this is a prophecy to that effect.
And the old man's charge to bury his bones beside this prophet's bones may be an indication of his repentance for his slackness and his lying to the man of God.
When you see God in the events around you and He makes His voice known to you, submit to Him and obey His commandments, to receive His blessing and power in your life.
Consecrated him: appointed him a priest by beginning the offering of a sacrifice to the idol.

It is certain that God's punishment of His prophet who came from Judah reached Jeroboam. And all these things, beginning with the prophecy at the pagan altar to the healing of his dried-up hand to the punishment of the man of God for disobeying the commandment, were all sufficient as a message from the Lord to Jeroboam to amend his ways, but unfortunately he did not benefit from the Lord's long-suffering and did not repent of his evil works, but continued to set up priests for the high places from outside the tribe of Levi, so that whoever desired the priesthood he made a priest. And these evils were the reasons for God's removing his kingdom and the destruction of his soul, for by these sins he judged himself.

And we notice in this chapter that all did not obey God, whether King Jeroboam, or the man of God, or the old man, and the only one who obeyed God was the lion. All went astray and became corrupt and wandered from God, and none remained obedient except the animals.
The death of Jeroboam and Rehoboam

entries.section: (1) The visit of Jeroboam's wife to Ahijah

paragraphs.text: After God warned Jeroboam to turn back from the worship of idols and he did not repent, He sent him a severe affliction, hoping it would awaken him: the illness of his son Abijah, who was perhaps his firstborn. This was contrary to his human arrangements, for he had been a successful administrative leader who had planned everything carefully in order to leave his kingdom to his son as an inheritance. Yet now the son falls ill and then dies, so that God might teach him that he must rely on Him and not on his own strength, and that he might turn from the worship of idols to God.

entries.section: (1) The visit of Jeroboam's wife to Ahijah

paragraphs.text: Shiloh: It lies south of Shechem and north of Jerusalem, and the tabernacle of God was there, so the prophet Ahijah and other believers who held fast to the worship of God and rejected idols dwelt in it. Jeroboam asked his wife to go to Shiloh to meet the prophet Ahijah, who had previously told him that he would reign over the people of Israel (ch. 11:29), and he asked her to disguise herself so that no one would know that he was resorting to the prophet.
We notice several matters in his asking his wife to disguise herself:

1- His awareness of his sins, which anger God, and of God's judgment upon them; yet he did not want to repent. He wanted only his own interests, namely reassurance about his son's recovery, and he feared that Ahijah would refuse to answer him.
2- Because he was deceitful and wicked, he did not trust any of his servants, so he sent his wife, since the son's recovery mattered to her as it did to him.
3- He believed that Ahijah was a prophet able to know the future by the power of God, yet in ignorance he thought he could deceive him by his wife's disguise.
4- He did not want his people to know that he was taking refuge with a prophet of God, because he did not want them to return to the temple of God and His prophets, lest they leave him and his idols.

5- In Jeroboam's heart there was faith that God alone is the true God, so he sent to learn His voice concerning the recovery of his son, and he did not ask his idols, because he did not believe in them, even though he had deceived his people and told them, "This is the image of God."

entries.section: (1) The visit of Jeroboam's wife to Ahijah

paragraphs.text: He asked her to take some simple gifts that were usually presented when meeting the prophets, as an expression of the honor due to them, for he is able to ask God, who would reveal to him the fate of his son.

entries.section: (1) The visit of Jeroboam's wife to Ahijah

paragraphs.text: His eyes were set: His eyes grew very weak, or he lost his sight completely.
Jeroboam's wife did what her husband had asked of her and went to the house of Ahijah in Shiloh, and Ahijah's sight had grown dim through old age.

entries.section: (1) The visit of Jeroboam's wife to Ahijah

paragraphs.text: The Lord informed him of the identity of the woman coming to him, of the reason for her coming, and that she would be disguised so that the prophet would not know who she was, and then He told him what to say. Thus we see that the power of God perfects His children however great their weakness, and even reveals to them what the strong cannot know. His inability to see did not prevent him from knowing the truth about the queen, the wife of Jeroboam, who was in disguise.

As long as you are with God, do not be troubled by any weakness that befalls you, for God is able to compensate you for it, so that you become stronger than the strong. He arranges your affairs, gives you all your needs, and reveals to you the greatest thing, which is His love and the knowledge of Him.

entries.section: (1) The visit of Jeroboam's wife to Ahijah

paragraphs.text: As soon as the Lord finished speaking to Ahijah, he sensed the woman's coming and heard the sound of her feet at the door, so he received her by name, saying to her, "O wife of Jeroboam." He told her that there was no need for disguise and that he had for her tidings that were not at all pleasant. Thus everyone who lies to God or deceives Him must expect an angry reaction from God, because he treats Him lightly.

entries.section: (1) The visit of Jeroboam's wife to Ahijah

paragraphs.text: Ahijah told Jeroboam's wife a message from God to her husband, in which He reminds him that it was He who raised him from being a fugitive in Egypt, despised, to the throne of Israel, and who tore the kingdom of David apart and gave him the greater part of it. God attributes the kingdom to David even though he had died and his grandson Jeroboam was reigning over it, because of David's piety, his keeping of God's commandments and his uprightness; therefore God blessed him and blessed the kingdom for his sake. But when Jeroboam sinned, he gave him a part of it and gave a part to Rehoboam. Yet Jeroboam learned nothing from the virtues of David and his piety; he did not worship God with all his heart, but walked in evil and worshiped idols.

Here we find that God calls Himself "the Lord God of Israel," for He still loves His people despite their departure from Him. He calls Himself their God in order to call them to repentance, but if they persist in their sins He will forsake them and leave the nations to discipline them.

God also reminded him that he had committed terrible sins, more than all who were before him. Solomon sinned by having many wives and honoring his wives by setting up idols for their gods, but he continued to worship God in His temple. Jeroboam, however, cut off his relation to worship in the temple of God and made idols, namely the golden calves, and claimed that they were his gods and the gods of the people, and he bowed down to them and even served as a priest to them.

entries.section: (1) The visit of Jeroboam's wife to Ahijah

paragraphs.text: Him that pisseth against the wall: every male.
Him that is shut up and left: the slaves and the free, or the imprisoned and the free; the meaning is everyone.
Dung: the waste of animals.

Then God pronounced His punishment on Jeroboam: that all his offspring and all the males, that is, those who could reign after him, would be destroyed, and He would be rid of them as a man is rid of the waste of animals. They would be killed and their corpses cast out, and no one would bury them because of the intensity of fear, for Baasha, the king who would come to the throne of Israel, would destroy all the offspring of Jeroboam (ch. 15:29). Just as Jeroboam rejected the worship of God and led his people astray, so God rejects him and destroys all his offspring.

entries.section: (1) The visit of Jeroboam's wife to Ahijah

paragraphs.text: The prophet asked Jeroboam's wife to return to her house, and he foretold to her that as soon as she entered the city her son would die.

entries.section: (1) The visit of Jeroboam's wife to Ahijah

paragraphs.text: The Lord found in Abijah the son of Jeroboam something good. Perhaps he rejected his father's idols and still prayed with his face toward Jerusalem, where the temple of God was. For this reason the Lord had mercy on him by his death, that he might be buried with honor and not be overtaken by the shame that would overtake his father and the rest of his family, as the Scripture says, "The righteous is taken away from the evil to come" (Isa 57:1).

entries.section: (1) The visit of Jeroboam's wife to Ahijah

paragraphs.text: That day: that is, very soon.

But what? even now: that is, God will not say more and is content with what He has said, because the execution will be swift. The Lord chooses for Himself another king whom He sets over Israel and who will cut off the house of Jeroboam, namely King Baasha. The Lord decreed that the time for the fulfillment of this prophecy would come very soon; for after the death of Jeroboam his son Nadab reigned for two years, and then Baasha rose against him and killed him and all the offspring of Jeroboam, and reigned in his place.

entries.section: (1) The visit of Jeroboam's wife to Ahijah

paragraphs.text: As a reed is shaken in the water: the reed is the cane, or the rush that is planted along watercourses, and because of its lightness it shakes violently when the winds blow upon it.
Beyond the river: that is, to Nineveh, which is on the river Euphrates, and all the cities of Assyria that belong to it.
Their groves: the plural of the grove, a tall piece of wood set up on high places for the worship of idols.

The divine punishment extends to the whole kingdom of Israel and not only to the offspring of Jeroboam, because all the kings of Israel walked in the worship of the idols that Jeroboam made. So the kingdom of Assyria attacked them and took them captive in three stages, 230 years after the reign of Jeroboam (2 Kgs 17), and at that time all the people of Israel will be in great distress, shaking like the shaking of a reed in the water. God takes the land of Canaan that He gave to His people and gives it to Assyria, while His people in the kingdom of Israel are scattered in the land of Assyria, especially since they went on and on in worshiping foreign gods, for the golden calves of Jeroboam encouraged them to worship many other gods.

entries.section: (2) The death of Jeroboam and his son

paragraphs.text: Tirzah: a city of beautiful appearance, lying northeast of Shechem at a distance of 11.5 km.

Jeroboam's wife returned to the king's residence in the city of Tirzah, to which he had moved from Shechem, the capital. Perhaps it was a resting place for the king because of its beauty and not a second capital. The king remained in Shechem and Tirzah until King Omri built the city of Samaria and moved the capital to it (ch. 16:23, 24). When the feet of Jeroboam's wife touched the threshold of the door, which may have been the gate of the city or the door of her house, her son died, and they buried him and made lamentation for him, as the prophet Ahijah had told her. The prophecy was fulfilled, and this was an incentive from God to Jeroboam and his house to repent of their sins, because the death of the boy announces that the rest of the prophecy would also be fulfilled. But sadly Jeroboam did not repent; he continued in the worship of idols and also made war against the kingdom of Judah (v. 19).

entries.section: (2) The death of Jeroboam and his son

paragraphs.text: Jeroboam walked in evil and entered into wars with Rehoboam and his son Abijah, the kings of Judah (v. 30, 2 Chr 13:3-20). In them Jeroboam was defeated and Abijah took from him many cities such as Bethel. Jeroboam reigned for 22 years, and then the Lord struck him with an illness and he died, and this shows God's anger against him. Then his son Nadab reigned for two years, and after him the family of Jeroboam came to an end, for all his offspring were killed, that the word of God which He spoke by the mouth of Ahijah might be fulfilled.
The book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel is not the book of Chronicles found in the Holy Bible, but a book in which the records of the kings of Israel were written.

Do not persist in evil and anger God, but learn from the events of life that pass over you, so that you may take heed and repent, for God desires your salvation. So return to Him, because He loves you.

entries.section: (3) The evils of Rehoboam, his wars and his death

paragraphs.text: While Jeroboam was reigning over ten tribes in Israel, Rehoboam the son of Solomon was reigning in Judah over two tribes (the tribe of Judah and the tribe of Benjamin). Rehoboam was 41 years old when he took the throne, and he reigned 17 years; the capital of his kingdom was Jerusalem, and his mother was "Naamah," who was of the children of Ammon. If Solomon reigned for 40 years, this means that he begot Rehoboam before he became king, so he was probably the firstborn, and the influence of his Gentile mother is evident, for he worshiped idols and built temples for them, as appears in the following verses, even though he was in Jerusalem, the city that God chose so that His temple and worship would be in it alone. God's choosing Jerusalem so that His name would be called upon it shows the enormity of the sin of Rehoboam, and before him of his father Solomon, in placing statues of foreign gods in it for the people to worship.

entries.section: (3) The evils of Rehoboam, his wars and his death

paragraphs.text: They provoked him to jealousy: they stirred up His jealousy, that is, they angered Him.

At that time the people of Judah were doing evil, and they angered the Lord more than all that their fathers had done, by their many sins. God likens His people to a bride and Himself to her bridegroom, so when she sins by worshiping other pagan gods she defies Him, angers Him and stirs up His jealousy as her bridegroom, and He becomes angry with her. This is what the kingdom of Judah did by worshiping idols in the days of Rehoboam, as will appear in the next two verses.

entries.section: (3) The evils of Rehoboam, his wars and his death

paragraphs.text: High places: altars on the tops of hills whose use God forbade (Deut 12:11, 13). Images: sacred pillars for the idols in the form of statues.

The people of God built for themselves, on the hills and under the trees, images and pillars for their pagan worship; that is, the pagan worship of the gods of heaven spread on the hills and under every tree that had great shade, so the pagan gods were many, and all this in the holy city of God, Jerusalem, and its surroundings. This shows how far the people had departed from the worship of God.

entries.section: (3) The evils of Rehoboam, his wars and his death

paragraphs.text: Sodomites: the passive partner in sexual perversion between two men.

In their worship of idols, and to please the gods, they practiced sexual perversion between men, and of course they also practiced fornication before that, so there were women and men consecrated to fornication in the temples of the pagan gods, and their earnings were given to the temples of the gods. This shows the depth of degradation to which the people of God had come, for they had become like the nations whom God drove out of the land of Canaan before His people dwelt in it.

Beware of leaving God and His Church and immersing yourself in the world and its lusts, for the teachings of the Church condemn you if you neglect them. Why do you sink into evil like the people of the world?! Be strong and walk uprightly, and you will be the light of the world and the salt of the earth, confident that God will support you and protect you.

entries.section: (4) Rehoboam and his wars against Shishak and against Jeroboam

paragraphs.text: Came up: because the land of Judah is higher than the land of Egypt.

In the fifth year of the reign of Rehoboam, Shishak came, the founder of the Twenty-second Dynasty in Egypt, and he was the most dangerous enemy to invade the land of Israel since the days of King Saul. Jeroboam had summoned him to support him and establish his power against Rehoboam king of Judah, so he attacked the kingdom of Judah and seized a number of its towns, and he also subdued some cities belonging to the northern kingdom, which were under the authority of the Canaanites, and gave them to his ally Jeroboam, who had lived in Egypt for a period of time under Shishak's protection. All this Shishak recorded on the walls of the temples of Karnak. This shows the departure of both the northern and southern kingdoms of the children of Israel from God and their reliance on the powers of the world, which caused God to forsake them, so they fell into trials. In Rehoboam's reign the kingdom was divided, and Jeroboam died of illness and his offspring were cut off, as we mentioned before, and here Shishak disciplines the people of God.

entries.section: (4) Rehoboam and his wars against Shishak and against Jeroboam

paragraphs.text: It was the custom of the people at that time to keep their jewels by depositing them in trust in the temple; so Shishak seized the treasures of the temple and the treasures of the royal palace, and he also took the shields of gold that Solomon had made.

If you are lax with sin, Satan will rob you of all the virtues and abilities you possess and humiliate you. So hold fast to your relationship with God, so that Satan may fear you, God may keep you, and you may live in peace.

entries.section: (4) Rehoboam and his wars against Shishak and against Jeroboam

paragraphs.text: The guard: the guards.

Since gold was not as plentiful in this period as it was in the days of Solomon, Rehoboam substituted shields of bronze for them and committed them to the hand of the guard of the royal palace. So whenever the king entered the temple, the soldiers would bring the shields there, and when the king departed they would return them to their storehouse.

entries.section: (4) Rehoboam and his wars against Shishak and against Jeroboam

paragraphs.text: The rest of the acts of Rehoboam and all that he did are written in "the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah." The book of chronicles meant is not the one found in the Holy Bible, but books in which the records of the kings were written, as some details about the life of Rehoboam were mentioned in the Second Book of Chronicles (2 Chr 10:12).

entries.section: (4) Rehoboam and his wars against Shishak and against Jeroboam

paragraphs.text: There was never any agreement between the two parts of the divided kingdom, Judah and Israel, throughout the reign of the two kings, Rehoboam in Judah and Jeroboam in Israel, for they remained continually in wars and disputes.

entries.section: (4) Rehoboam and his wars against Shishak and against Jeroboam

paragraphs.text: Rehoboam died and was buried with his fathers in the city of David. His mother was "Naamah the Ammonitess." His son Abijam, who is also called "Abijah," succeeded him on the throne.
The First Book of Kings. Abijah and Asa reign over Judah, and Nadab and Baasha over Israel

entries.section: (1) Abijam the son of Rehoboam, king over Judah

paragraphs.text: Abijam: He is also called Abijah (2 Chr 13:1). The reign of Jeroboam king of Israel was twenty-two years (ch. 14:20). Abijam ascended the throne of Judah in the eighteenth year of the reign of Jeroboam, and he continued to reign only three years. That is, Abijam king of Judah and Jeroboam king of Israel reigned at the same time for three years, and after the three years the reign of Jeroboam extended another year, during which he was a contemporary of Abijam's successor, Asa king of Judah.

entries.section: (1) Abijam the son of Rehoboam, king over Judah

paragraphs.text: The capital of his kingdom was Jerusalem, in which he reigned three years. His mother was Maachah, the granddaughter of Absalom the son of David (a granddaughter is often called a daughter), and Absalom was the son of David who led a revolt and drove his father out of the kingdom, so he was wicked, and his granddaughter Maachah was wicked like him. Abijam was not the firstborn of Rehoboam, but the son of Maachah, whom Rehoboam loved, and who is also called Michaiah in (2 Chr 13:2). Because she was strong in personality, she influenced the kingdom and set her son Abijam on the throne as king.

entries.section: (1) Abijam the son of Rehoboam, king over Judah

paragraphs.text: This verse describes very briefly the summary of what characterized the reign of Abijam: he followed the steps of his father Rehoboam, and his heart was not with God as was the heart of David his forefather, but he fell into the worship of idols and all the evils connected with it. This shows the influence of wicked fathers upon their children.

entries.section: (1) Abijam the son of Rehoboam, king over Judah

paragraphs.text: It is an Eastern custom to keep a lamp burning continually in the house, never put out unless the master of the house dies and the house is abandoned. Here God shows how He gave a lamp to David: although Rehoboam and his son Abijam were wicked, God gave Abijam a righteous son, Asa.
